noticias.titulo: Trump criticises Schumer amid push for new Democrat leadership in US Senate
noticias.resumen: Schumer, who has led the Democrats since 2017, faces a challenge from Chris Van Hollen in his bid for majority leader.
noticias.texto:
Trump criticises Schumer amid push for new Democrat leadership in US Senate
Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus since 2017, faces a challenge from Chris Van Hollen in his bid to be the next Senate majority leader.
Chuck Schumer, the top Democrat in the United States Senate, is facing backlash against his bid to serve as Senate majority leader in the incoming Congress.
On Sunday, President Donald Trump added to the ongoing criticism of Schumer’s leadership, signalling there would be tension with the White House if Schumer were picked again to lead the Democratic caucus.
“It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority Leader,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
“He failed badly as ‘Leader’ once before, one of the worst in history, and I have little doubt that he will fail again.”
The debate over Schumer’s leadership has underscored divides within the Democratic Party, particularly in the wake of the November 3 midterm elections.
Following a historic set of victories, Democrats are set to take control of both chambers of Congress in January.
Schumer, who leads the Democratic Senate minority, is hoping to retain his leadership position. A closed-door, secret-ballot vote is scheduled for December 1 to decide the majority leader.
A senator representing New York since 1999, Schumer has expressed confidence in his odds, saying he has the necessary votes to stay in charge.
“I will be elected majority leader,” Schumer told reporters last week.
But critics say Schumer, who will turn 76 on Monday, is ill-suited to lead a Senate Democratic caucus increasingly shaped by younger, anti-establishment lawmakers.
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen, backed by progressives, has mounted a campaign to challenge Schumer for the majority leader role.
Van Hollen told NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday that he, too, was confident of winning.
“If you look at our caucus, you can see a huge appetite for change. They are seeing the American people and the Democratic Party calling for change. They also want to change the way we do business in the United States Democratic caucus and the United States Senate,” he said.
Schumer has also seen falling public approval ratings. In mid-November, a poll by the news agency Reuters and the research firm Ipsos found that 34 percent of self-identified Democrats viewed Schumer favourably. That percentage was down from 38 percent in February.
November’s poll also suggested that 43 percent of Democrats held an unfavourable view of Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats since 2017.
The Senate Democratic leader is the only unresolved role among Congress’s top four positions.
House Democrats last week nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be speaker in the next Congress.
Meanwhile, John Thune will continue to lead Senate Republicans, and Representative Jim Jordan will succeed Speaker Mike Johnson as the top House Republican.

noticias.titulo: Trump to host private dinner for largest owners of his meme coin
noticias.resumen: Sunday's dinner is the third event for top holders of the $Trump meme coin, launched shortly before his inauguration.
noticias.texto:
Trump to host private dinner for largest owners of his meme coin
Sunday’s dinner is the third private event for top holders of the $Trump meme coin, launched shortly before his second inauguration.
United States President Donald Trump will host a third private dinner for top investors in his meme coin $TRUMP, reigniting questions about potential conflicts of interest with his cryptocurrency ventures.
Sunday’s gala will take place at the Trump National Golf Club outside Washington, DC.
According to the dinner’s official website, the top 185 meme-coin holders will be invited to a gala dinner, where guests will include businessman Kevin O’Leary and boxer Floyd Mayweather.
The top 29 holders, meanwhile, will be given special access to a VIP reception where Trump will reportedly be present.
“There will be no private meetings with The President. No gifts will be accepted,” the website said of the VIP reception.
The event has been billed as “a once-in-a-lifetime experience — an evening you will talk about forever”.
But Democrats have accused the Republican leader of leveraging his public office for profit in violation of federal law. They see such dinners as an opportunity for private interests to pay for access to the president.
“Trump is continuing to exploit the presidency for his personal gain,” Kendall Witmer, the deputy communications director for the Democratic National Committee, said in a statement.
In October, shortly after the gala was announced, eight Democratic senators issued an open letter promising to investigate any conflicts of interest such an event might raise.
“President Trump’s continued monetization of his name and likeness once again raises serious ethical concerns, necessitating this request for a robust inquiry into the President’s financial entanglements and personal profiteering,” the letter said.
The Democratic Party has since won majorities in both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterm race, paving the way for possible inquiries and subpoenas when the new members are sworn in next year.
Trump’s White House has dismissed the criticism, calling the dinner a “private event, not a government function”. It has also emphasised that “there is no promise of official government action in exchange for attending”.
Trump has also argued that many of his assets are held in a trust while he is in office, though that trust is largely run by his family members.
The president is a stakeholder in cryptocurrency firms like World Liberty Financial, and has made promoting cryptocurrency a central part of his second term.
Under his leadership, the US Treasury established a reserve of digital currency assets, as part of Trump’s effort to make the US the “crypto capital of the world”.
Sunday’s gala is believed to be the third such dinner for top $Trump meme coin holders.
Meme coins trade on a popular likeness from the internet. Trump launched his on January 17, 2025, days before the start of his second term.
To encourage meme-coin purchases, Trump and his business partners held private events on May 22, 2025, and again on April 25, 2026, for top holders of the cryptocurrency.
The first was held at the same Trump golf club outside Washington, DC, and the second took place at Mar-a-Lago, Trump’s Florida resort.
The May 2025 dinner reportedly required a minimum of $55,000 in $Trump coins to attend.
At the time, Chinese crypto investor Justin Sun was declared the winner of a “contest” for who held the most $TRUMP coins. Sun held about $18m of the coin in 2025, as well as tokens from World Liberty Financial.
Earlier this year, Sun sued World Liberty Financial, saying it had frozen his access to the assets he owned with it, making it impossible for him to sell them.
Trump’s inauguration in January 2025 proved a major boost for his coin, pushing its value to $74.
The $Trump coin has since lost value. On the eve of the gala dinner, it is worth about $0.88.
According to financial disclosure forms released earlier this year, Trump earned more than $2.2bn in 2025, the first year of his second term.
Much of that wealth came from meme coins, tokens and other digital assets. Some $636m came from $Trump meme coin sales.

noticias.titulo: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 with North Carolina seat
noticias.resumen: At least 258 US House seats are now under Democratic control, with four more midterm races yet to be decided.
noticias.texto:
Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 with North Carolina seat
At least 258 US House seats are now under Democratic control, with four more midterm races yet to be decided.
The Democratic Party has won at least 258 seats in the United States House of Representatives, its highest total since 1992.
On Sunday, a congressional race in North Carolina was decided after a recount, giving Democrats their 258th House seat, as a handful of races in the 2026 midterm elections are still being counted.
The race for North Carolina’s 5th congressional district saw Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeat Republican incumbent Virginia Foxx, who has served 11 terms in Congress.
The win was symbolic of a larger political shift in North Carolina and elsewhere, as longtime Republican strongholds flipped to Democratic hands, sometimes for the first time in decades.
Foxx was first elected in 2004, and in recent years, she was the chair of the House Rules Committee. According to The Associated Press news agency, only 330 votes separated Hubbard and Foxx as of Sunday, when the race was called in the Democrat’s favour.
Four House races have yet to be called, meaning Democrats may still expand their already sizeable majority in the 435-member House.
The party has now picked up about 47 House seats. Currently, in the outgoing Congress, Democrats hold 214 seats.
But the House was not the only congressional chamber to flip in this year’s midterm elections.
In the 120th Congress, set to be sworn in on January 3, Democrats will also hold 56 seats in the US Senate, its largest majority in more than a decade.
Those majorities give the Democratic Party significant power over legislation, although President Donald Trump, a Republican, has already pledged to veto bills the party puts forward.
Experts say the Republican Party’s drubbing in the midterm elections was driven by voter frustration with issues like the cost of living, the US-Israel war on Iran, corruption and immigration raids.
It was also widely interpreted as a referendum on Trump’s second term, which began in 2025.
As of November, only 32 percent of Americans approved of Trump’s job performance, according to a poll by the news agency Reuters and the research firm Ipsos.
Democrats have framed their electoral victory as a unique opportunity to shape the final two years of Trump’s presidency.
Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a progressive who won her re-election bid in New York’s 14th congressional district, called the political shift a “mandate for change”.
“This is a historic moment for our country. This is one of the largest classes we have seen,” Ocasio-Cortez said at the US Capitol.
The party’s majority in the House will be larger than any since Democrat Bill Clinton was first elected president in 1992 with a 258-seat majority for his party.
It is also just above the 257 seats held by Democrats when Barack Obama was elected in 2008.

noticias.titulo: Beau Lamarre-Condon acted like a ‘poorly behaved boyfriend’ before alleged double murders, defence argues
noticias.resumen: Crown says accused developed ‘jealous obsession’ but defence says ‘love makes fools of us’ Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Beau Lamarre-Condon acted like a “poorly behaved boyfriend” before allegedly murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, a court has heard. Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting the Sydney couple with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024. Continue reading...
noticias.texto:
Beau Lamarre-Condon acted like a “poorly behaved boyfriend” before allegedly murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, a court has heard.
Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting the Sydney couple with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
The former officer has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter, claiming the two men died while he acted in “self-defence”.
Lamarre-Condon developed a “jealous obsession” with Baird when two were casually and non-exclusively dating in late 2022 and 2023, the prosecution argued.
The accused has admitted to going through Baird’s phone to delete and block other men, entering the Paddington home one night and running off with Baird’s wallet and phone, and watching Baird have sex with another man through his bedroom window.
But in his closing statement to the New South Wales supreme court, defence barrister John Stratton SC claimed this was because he had fallen “head over heels” in love with Baird.
“Love makes fools of us all and you certainly might think that that very much applies to all of us whether young or old, straight or gay, male or female,” Stratton said.
“There’s no doubt the accused Beau Lamarre-Condon did plenty of foolish things and you might think the level of them was unusual, that he was a poorly behaved boyfriend.
“There’s a long distance between his admitting that sort of behaviour, and you finding him guilty of murder.”
But crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC urged the jury to reject Lamarre-Condon’s account and convict him on all three counts, as he wrapped up his closing statement on Monday.
Driven by his jealous obsession, the accused drove to Paddington in a hired car, waited for his opportunity, entered the house with a gun loaded with stolen bullets, and shot Baird in the back and temple, Hatfield alleged.
“It was not self-defence or an accident,” he told the New South Wales supreme court.
“The evidence speaks only to an execution.”
Lamarre-Condon had testified he shot Baird after he lunged at him with a knife.
During this struggle, his gun was then flung across the room and picked up by Davies before the officer grabbed his arm and pushed the gun towards Davies.
Davies then pulled the trigger and shot himself, Lamarre-Condon told the court.
But this defence rests entirely on his own account and even if Baird had picked up a knife, it would not have assisted him against a Glock pistol, Hatfield said.
“You might think he is a proven and persistent liar and such a scenario is completely contrary to the weight of the evidence,” he told the court.
“The accused’s account is not the truth. It is a story made up after the fact in an attempt to meet the evidence.”
But Stratton said there were two serious problems with the crown case about Davies’ death that the prosecution “hasn’t overcome and can never overcome”.
Though Davies’ DNA was found on the trigger of the gun, there was no blood, the jury heard. Davies being the source of the majority of DNA on this part of the gun is “powerful” evidence his finger was on the trigger when the third shot was fired, Stratton said.
The prosecution also failed to locate the bullet or any bullet fragments of the shot that struck Davies, and this is enough to leave jurors with reasonable doubt about the crown case, the barrister said.
“The forensic and ballistic evidence makes it more likely that the accused’s version is true, than the version the crown seeks to persuade,” he told the court.
The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

noticias.titulo: Former Bachelor star Sam Wood seeking mediation amid DV charges for allegedly strangling wife
noticias.resumen: Lawyer Brad Hill seeks two-week adjournment on Monday for mediation, which can only occur if alleged victim consents Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Former reality TV star Sam Wood is seeking mediation amid his serious domestic violence charges for allegedly strangling his wife. The Melbourne-based fitness influencer has made the request days after his distressed prison call, asking to speak to his wife, was heard in court. Continue reading...
noticias.texto:
Former reality TV star Sam Wood is seeking mediation amid his serious domestic violence charges for allegedly strangling his wife.
The Melbourne-based fitness influencer has made the request days after his distressed prison call, asking to speak to his wife, was heard in court.
Wood, 46, has spent seven weeks in custody since being arrested during a family holiday in Noosa.
He is accused of strangling his wife, Snezana, whom he met on Network Ten’s hit reality show The Bachelor in 2015.
Wood did not appear at Maroochydore magistrates court on Monday when his lawyer, Brad Hill, sought a two-week adjournment, proposing justice mediation to the prosecution.
Justice mediation in Queensland provides a chance for the alleged offender and victim to discuss the matter, but can only occur if the latter consents.
Wood’s matter was adjourned until 7 December and he remains in custody.
It came after a court heard a phone call Wood made from jail to his father saying: “I need to be able to talk to my wife”.
The call was played when his request for release reached Queensland’s court of appeal on 17 November after two lower courts had denied him bail.
“There is no way she would want this,” Wood told his father, Andrew, in the 30 October call.
“We had a bad fight but, if she thought I was going to jail, there would be no way.”
A highly distressed Wood discussed in the call activities that could breach his proposed bail conditions, including a ban on contacting Snezana.
“If she changes her statement, the police would not have a leg to stand on,” he said, at times sobbing.
Justice David Boddice said at the latest bail application Wood could be heard discussing his wife making a statutory declaration that the alleged choking did not happen.
“That is classic interfering with witnesses,” he said.
A decision on bail has been reserved.
An earlier hearing was told Wood allegedly shut a door between himself and Snezana, and her daughter Eve Markoski-Wood, while they were on holiday in Noosa on 3 October.
He then allegedly grabbed his wife by the throat and pushed her against the wall.
“She felt his grip become tighter. It’s alleged the complainant couldn’t breathe any more and couldn’t yell out for help,” Justice Patrick McCafferty said in his 30 October decision to deny Wood bail.
It was alleged Wood told Snezana and her daughter they could both die.
Wood earned a national profile as a star of The Bachelor’s third season in 2015, launching a successful home fitness business, 28 by Sam Wood.
He reportedly sold it in 2022 for more than $70m but remained the face of the online platform.
The platform was rebranded in late October, removing all references to Wood.
Snezana also built her own large profile, gaining more than 330,000 followers on Instagram. She has not posted since the alleged assault.

noticias.titulo: Tributes flow for Molly Meldrum: Anthony Albanese, Jason Donovan and others remember music industry great
noticias.resumen: Peter Andre, Richard Wilkins and Kate Ceberano share memories of ‘a truly unique character’ and ‘the fan all artists wish to have’ Molly Meldrum, Countdown host and promoter of Australian music, dies aged 83 Molly Meldrum – a life in pictures Ian ‘Molly’ Meldrum – obituary Friends and fans of Molly Meldrum have remembered the music industry great, who died on Monday at the age of 83 . Meldrum spent more than a decade hosting the ABC music show Countdown, leaving a lasting legacy on the Australian music landscape. Continue reading...
noticias.texto:
Friends and fans of Molly Meldrum have remembered the music industry great, who died on Monday at the age of 83.
Meldrum spent more than a decade hosting the ABC music show Countdown, leaving a lasting legacy on the Australian music landscape.
Anthony Albanese was among those paying tribute. “With an interview style that was inimitable and an enthusiasm that was uncontainable, Molly Meldrum loved music almost as much as we loved him,” the wrote in a post on X.
“On Countdown and beyond, he championed Australian artists and brought international acts to our shores. He gave new artists a leg up and established artists a welcoming embrace. And over the years as he implored us to do ourselves a favour, he became a central part of the Australian soundtrack. We were lucky to have him. May Ian ‘Molly’ Meldrum rest in peace.”
Jason Donovan said Meldrum was the “very heart” of the music program while he was growing up, calling the man a “truly unique character, a great Australian and one of this country’s greatest pioneers and ambassadors for music and entertainment”.
“He was loved, recognised and respected around the world for the extraordinary contribution he made to Australian music and the artists he championed,” Donovan wrote on Facebook. “There will never be another quite like him.”
The former Neighbours star shared a memory of Meldrum appearing on an episode alongside Kylie Minogue and Guy Pearce, adding: “What a day that was!”
The television presenter Richard Wilkins remembered his longtime friend on-air on Monday morning. The pair used to travel around the world for interviews, Wilkins said, which led to great memories and hilarious stories.
“Australian music would not be Australian music without Molly’s incredible contribution,” Wilkins said. “I shared so many overseas trips with Molly, which was a joy and a curse. He lost 13 passports, that was the tally I got to.
“We went from a Michael Jackson gig in Munich to see Bruce Springsteen in Paris. That was the sort of thing we used to get up to back in the day.”
Gavin Wood, a longtime friend of Meldrum’s who worked on Countdown, said the host was “one of the craziest, most colourful, funniest and most beautiful people you could ever have the pleasure of meeting”.
“What he has done for the Australian music industry is simply phenomenal,” Wood wrote. “His contribution, passion, enthusiasm and unwavering commitment to Australian artists helped shape an entire generation of music and entertainment.
“There will never be another Molly Meldrum. You simply cannot measure anyone against him.”
Bands and artists echoed those sentiments.
Meldrum produced Russell Morris’s 1969 single the Real Thing, which reached #1 on the charts. “He was a unique, and loveable individual,” Morris wrote on Facebook. “I was lucky enough to call him my friend, and mentor. The journey we went on was pretty surreal – his creative energy and insights were exceptional … He achieved things that were truly great. Things that sometimes seemed impossible.”
“He was such a huge presence in the Australian music industry and was a great friend and supporter of so many up and coming bands and artists – ourselves included,” the band Human Nature wrote. “Thanks for everything Molly. Rest easy.”
The singer Peter Andre posted a photo with Meldrum, praising him for helping to elevate his career and saying “this really hurts”.
“If it wasn’t for this man, I would not of had any of the chances I had to make it in any way in the entertainment industry back when it was near impossible to get noticed,” Andre wrote. “He believed in me from day one and I am forever grateful to Ian ‘Molly’ Meldrum.”
Kate Ceberano wrote: “He had no agenda he wanted, no praise, he never basked in any reflected glory or self pride. He simply wanted the world to hear what he could hear, wanted you to see what he was looking at and then blow it up to 11. Way up sky high. No dream is too big. No cringe, withholding nothing.
“He was the fan all artists wish to have.”
Iva Davies of Icehouse also paid tribute: “He was such a bright, larger than life figure in our Australian music scene for so many years … Like the rest of the music community that owed so much to his support, the band and I are so thankful that Molly was a part of our lives and music. There will never be another like him and he will be sorely missed by so many.”
In an interview with 2GB, Marcia Hines said: “I considered Molly a friend, a dear, dear friend, and an advocate for our music … He believed in us. That’s what he did for us. He believed in all of us … We’ve lost such an incredible person in our industry.”
She continued: “What you saw was what you got. That was really Molly. He fumbled. He laughed. He laughed at himself. But most importantly he loved us.”
The Australian Recording Industry Association issued its own praise of Meldrum’s work, noting that both he and the Countdown program were the first inductees into the Aria Hall of Fame who weren’t recording artists, back in 2014.
“It is impossible to imagine what Australian music would look like without Molly’s long and storied career,” said Annabelle Herd, Aria’s chief executive. “He shaped the music taste of a generation of Australians and gave so much of himself for the good of Australian artists, for which our whole industry is eternally grateful.”
The St Kilda football club remembered Meldrum as a “lifelong Sainter”, saying the organisation was deeply saddened by his death.
“An iconic and passionate supporter of our football club, Molly changed and brightened the lives of so many across a storied career,” the club wrote on Facebook.

noticias.titulo: Molly Meldrum, Countdown host and promoter of Australian music, dies aged 83
noticias.resumen: Much-loved broadcaster played a critical role in exposing rest of the world to Australian music – and vice versa Tributes flow for Molly Meldrum: Human Nature, Jason Donovan and others remember music industry great Molly Meldrum – a life in pictures Ian ‘Molly’ Meldrum – obituary Molly Meldrum, the Australian music journalist, broadcaster and producer, has died at the age of 83. He died peacefully in the early hours of Monday morning at a hospital in Melbourne, his longtime friend and manager, Mark Klemens, confirmed to the Guardian. Continue reading...
noticias.texto:
Molly Meldrum, the Australian music journalist, broadcaster and producer, has died at the age of 83.
He died peacefully in the early hours of Monday morning at a hospital in Melbourne, his longtime friend and manager, Mark Klemens, confirmed to the Guardian.
“We have lost a true Australian icon, a man who opened doors for so many and entertained millions of people here and around the world,” Klemens said.
“He was unconventional and wonderfully unpredictable, but always caring, always funny and always down to earth, with a passion the rest of us could only envy. He made the most of his life, and boy, was it a full one. Rest in peace, Molly.”
Meldrum’s partner, Yan Wongngam, and family said in a statement issued by Klemens: “Affectionately dubbed ‘the Guru’, Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music. He shaped not only the sound of a nation but also the dreams of generations who grew up with his voice guiding them..
“Yan cared for Molly with great love and devotion, especially through his final years. The family is deeply grateful to him, to Molly’s many loyal friends, and to the staff at Epworth Richmond for their wonderful care.”
The Stetson-wearing Countdown presenter is credited with engineering the breakthrough of Abba, Blondie and Madonna in Australia. During his time on the wildly popular Sunday evening ABC music show from 1974 to 1987, he championed songs including Blondie’s In the Flesh, John Mellencamp’s I Need a Lover, Duran Duran’s Planet Earth and Madonna’s Holiday, transforming then unknown tracks into Top 10 hits in Australia.
Meldrum also passionately promoted Australian performers, giving exposure on Countdown to dozens who went on to local or international fame, including INXS, Kylie Minogue, Skyhooks and Mental as Anything.
In a post on X, the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, paid tribute to Meldrum: “With an interview style that was inimitable and an enthusiasm that was uncontainable, Molly Meldrum loved music almost as much as we loved him. On Countdown and beyond, he championed Australian artists and brought international acts to our shores. He gave new artists a leg up and established artists a welcoming embrace. And over the years as he implored us to do ourselves a favour, he became a central part of the Australian soundtrack. We were lucky to have him.”
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll said Meldrum will be given a state funeral. “All of our thoughts as Victorians and indeed Australians are with Molly Meldrum’s family and his friends, and we know how wide that network was,” he said.
Elton John once described Meldrum as the “single most important influence in Australian pop music”.
Meldrum never disguised his unabashed fervour as a fan, even while forming decades-long friendships with an array of global stars.
He developed an obsession with the Beatles after their explosion on to the world stage, and eventually interviewed his pop idol, John Lennon, who fed him the scoop of the band’s impending break-up. But Meldrum did nothing with the incendiary information because he “was so in awe” of Lennon.
Born Ian Meldrum in Orbost, Victoria, to a family he called “quite dysfunctional”, the larger-than-life character moved to live with an aunt and uncle in Shepparton from the age of 12. He went from wanting to be a conductor to becoming entranced with the idea of producing music and later lived with the family of his close friend, the singer Ronnie Burns.
He was one of the first openly gay personalities on Australian television and was known for his bumbling interview technique and for his chaotic and colourful scuffles. On the 40th anniversary of Countdown in 2014, Prince Charles recalled a shambolic 1977 interview with Meldrum, telling the ABC: “There is an old show business saying which warns never to work with animals or children, but nobody prepared me for Molly Meldrum.”
Meldrum began appearing on camera on Countdown in mid-1975, delivering the weekly Rock Report, redubbed Humdrum by a guest host, John Paul Young. While reviewing albums, Meldrum would often hold LPs up awkwardly, making them hard to see under the glare of stage lights. ABC policy prohibited hosts endorsing products, so “do yourself a favour” became Meldrum’s catchphrase.
In the 1980s Meldrum landed various presenting gigs on television: the 1985 Oz for Africa concert, the Australian leg of Live Aid; the ABC interview show The Meldrum Tapes and a regular music segment, Molly’s Melodrama, on the variety show Hey Hey It’s Saturday.
In 2011 Meldrum fell from a ladder in the back yard of his Melbourne home and was placed in intensive care in a critical condition, undergoing surgery for head and spinal injuries. After four months he recovered enough to begin appearing in public again.
In 1986 he was made a member of the Order of Australia, with a citation for “service to the fostering of international relief and to youth”. In 2012 he was inducted into the Logie Hall of Fame. In 2014, when Meldrum became the first non-recording artist to be inducted into the Aria Hall of Fame, Minogue said the Australian music industry was “blessed to have had you in our lives for over four decades”.
Elton John was similarly unreserved in his praise, saying in 2019: “I don’t think anyone has done more for music in Australia than Molly Meldrum.”
Meldrum is survived by his partner, Yan Wongngam, his adopted son and his two younger brothers.

noticias.titulo: Manchester’s Co-op Live arena evacuated after apparent tear gas incident at Don Toliver concert
noticias.resumen: Incident occurred near the end of Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver, with one person taken to hospital Police have evacuated Manchester’s Co-op Live arena after a substance believed to be teargas was let off in the crowd during a Don Toliver concert. Greater Manchester police said the incident occurred near the end of the US rapper’s show on Sunday evening. Continue reading...
noticias.texto:
Police have evacuated Manchester’s Co-op Live arena after a substance believed to be teargas was let off in the crowd during a Don Toliver concert.
Greater Manchester police said the incident occurred near the end of the US rapper’s show on Sunday evening.
Greater Manchester police said concertgoers had been safely evacuated, with several people being assessed on site for side effects as a precaution and inquiries under way to determine what the substance was. No serious injuries have been reported.
Assistant chief constable Steph Parker said in a statement: “Our priority was to ensure the safety of every person that was attending the concert.
“Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time. Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital.
“We understand the concern that this incident will have raised – particularly those with loved ones at the venue last night – and we’d like to thank everyone for their patience as we dealt with it.
“There were over 12,000 people in attendance during this concert who were safely escorted from the arena so they could make their way home.”
She continued: “Our declaration of a major incident has allowed us to ensure emergency services and partner agencies can work together quickly and effectively to coordinate a safe response.
“We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about.”
The north-west ambulance service said one person was taken to hospital and more than 50 were assessed by clinicians.
The service said in a statement: “We deployed several emergency crews, including our Hazardous Area Response Team, to support the safe assessment and treatment of people at the scene.
“More than 50 people have been assessed by our clinicians, with some reporting eye and respiratory symptoms. Decontamination is being carried out as a precaution and one patient has been taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment.
“The incident remains ongoing and our teams remain at the scene assessing and caring for patients. We continue to work closely with emergency service partners while inquiries are carried out to establish what the substance was.
“Anyone at tonight’s event who has since noticed side effects or become ill should seek medical advice.”
Footage shared on social media appeared to show concertgoers coughing and covering their mouths as they left the venue.
Co-op Live has the capacity to hold 23,500 people, with American singer Phoebe Bridgers scheduled to perform at the venue on Thursday.
Don Toliver is partway through the UK leg of his Octane World Tour.

noticias.titulo: Video of ICE detaining father and daughter while boarding flight sparks protests in Seattle
noticias.resumen: Footage of Saturday incident, filmed by fellow passengers, quickly went viral on social media as mayor calls tactics ‘un-American’ Protesters marched through the Seattle-Tacoma international airport on Sunday after widely shared footage captured masked immigration agents detaining a father and daughter on an airport jet bridge as they boarded their Alaska Airlines flight. Video of the incident on Saturday – filmed by fellow passengers – quickly went viral on social media, sparking condemnation from lawmakers, including Washington Democratic governor Bob Ferguson and Seattle mayor Katie Wilson.
noticias.texto:
Protesters marched through the Seattle-Tacoma international airport on Sunday after widely shared footage captured masked immigration agents detaining a father and daughter on an airport jet bridge as they boarded their Alaska Airlines flight.
Video of the incident on Saturday – filmed by fellow passengers – quickly went viral on social media, sparking condemnation from lawmakers, including Washington Democratic governor Bob Ferguson and Seattle mayor Katie Wilson.
Footage and photographs showed protesters with bullhorns and signs that read “ICE out of Washington” and “Abolish ICE” at the Seattle airport. Protesters could be seen walking inside and around the airport chanting “ICE out now” and other rallying cries.
“I made my view very clear to Alaska Airlines: They need to call on ICE to get out of our airports,” Ferguson said in a briefing. “I’ll be making that request of every other airline that operates at SeaTac airport as well.”
On Sunday a lawyer representing Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and his daughter, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, said they were heading to a family baptism ceremony in California when they were detained by masked agents.
Other passengers boarding the Alaska Airlines flight at Seattle-Tacoma international airport used their cellphones to film the father and daughter being detained by the officers, who were wearing unmarked jackets and khaki pants.
The videos show the officers struggling with someone on the ground. The flight, bound for Los Angeles, was delayed.
ICE has stepped up operations at airports since the summer as the agency has shifted tactics from sweeping urban raids to more targeted operations in all corners of US, with arrests reaching record levels.
Ferguson called ICE’s tactics “deeply un-American” and called for the agency’s abolition.
“The video is horrific and it is chilling,” Ferguson said at a news conference on Saturday with labor leaders and local elected officials.
Wilson called ICE’s tactics “unacceptable and un-American”.
In a statement to the Guardian, ICE said its officers detained Mendoza, an immigrant from Mexico, who it said had overstayed his visa “in violation of our nation’s laws”.
According to the ICE statement, Mejia “hurled hot coffee on the officers”. ICE said she was in the US illegally from Mexico and had overstayed her visa. She could be charged with assaulting a federal officer.
The father and daughter were travelling to attend a baptism and were seeking asylum in the US, where they had lived since 2015, their lawyer, Olia Catala, told the Associated Press. They had no criminal record, Catala said.
Mejia, who is in her mid-20s, had married a US citizen and filed paperwork for adjustment of her status, the attorney said. Mejia’s husband – who was not detained -was accompanying Mejia and her father when they were detained on Saturday, Catala added.
“They’ve done everything correctly, and these are educated people,” Catala said of the father and daughter. “She went to college, to university, she worked for a nonprofit. No criminal history [for] any of them. So it’s just heartbreaking.”
Both were being held at the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma, Catala said.
She said Mejia was carrying a cup of coffee when the confrontation occurred. “When somebody’s charging at you, you’re going to drop a cup of coffee,” Catala said.
“It was just a lot of commotion, and honestly, if somebody is running at you or charging at you and they’re not wearing a uniform, you don’t know who they are,” Catala said. “There was a lot of panic, chaos, not knowing what’s going on.”
Alaska Airlines said ICE officers gave no advance notice of the enforcement action, which occurred during a busy travel weekend ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. The airline said it was working with the Port of Seattle, which manages the airport, to see if protocols were followed, and had raised concerns “directly with the appropriate authorities”.
The Port of Seattle said in a statement that the arrest was distressing not only for the family but for other passengers, and that local authorities would “engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred”.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

noticias.titulo: US army to blow up bomb-making chemicals despite safety concerns
noticias.resumen: Army invokes emergency provisions in Iowa to avoid court order despite worries about health and environment risks The US army plans to invoke emergency provisions to avoid a court order that had put on hold plans to detonate several tons of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa , saying that continued delays will make it more dangerous as the weather starts to turn colder. “To protect its personnel and the surrounding communities, the Army needs to take swift action,” government lawyers told the eight US circuit court of appeals in a filing late on Saturday. “Protection of human health and the environ
noticias.texto:
The US army plans to invoke emergency provisions to avoid a court order that had put on hold plans to detonate several tons of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa, saying that continued delays will make it more dangerous as the weather starts to turn colder.
“To protect its personnel and the surrounding communities, the Army needs to take swift action,” government lawyers told the eight US circuit court of appeals in a filing late on Saturday. “Protection of human health and the environment demand action now, not delay.”
The army plans to detonate the chemicals by Tuesday.
Environmental groups criticized the government’s move, decrying it as a maneuver to get around a court order and avoid public demands for safety and transparency.
The appeals court on Thursday granted a request by environmentalists to put on hold a permit that cleared the way for the detonation in Middletown, a small community about 160 miles (257km) south-east of Des Moines. It was initially planned for Friday, but the army later announced that it would push the operation to Monday after an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.
Environmentalists have called for a review of the emergency permit that was approved earlier this month by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
In a statement on Sunday, the Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club and Earthjustice questioned claims that all alternatives were given appropriate consideration.
“The Army seemed more concerned over the weekend with finding a way to sidestep the judicial process than on meeting the public’s demands for greater transparency, notice to affected communities, and far stronger protection of people, property, and the environment from serious harm,” said Thien Chau, an attorney at Earthjustice.
Government lawyers said the army doesn’t need a permit to take emergency action against an immediate threat from explosive material.
They said the standards of a federal law regulating hazardous waste don’t apply in situations when there is an immediate threat to health, safety or the environment as determined by an explosive or munitions emergency response specialist.
Officials contend that the chemicals are unstable, and the risk of an uncontrolled explosion is growing, particularly as temperatures drop. They said there is a risk that the chemicals may explode as temperatures are expected to drop below 30F (-1C) in the coming days.
In March, staff at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant found several dozen barrels of degraded lead azide, which is used in munitions production. Crystallization of the material created an unstable and dangerous situation, prompting the army to assemble experts in munitions chemistry, engineering and environmental safety to come up with a plan.
According to EPA documents, alternatives such as neutralizing and decomposing the drums’ contents with other chemicals were considered. But officials said handling the drums would increase the probability of an accidental, fatal detonation.
The environmental groups disagreed, arguing in their petition that other alternatives were not fully considered. They also criticized officials for not sharing more information with the public.
Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, but thousands more in surrounding areas could be affected by detonated material that could disperse in the air and land on the ground.
Iowans in the region were told to stay inside, keep windows and doors closed, bring pets and livestock indoors, and clean cars, windowsills and outdoor surfaces after.
“The detonation will result in an air plume with some lead-containing particles which will disperse in the air and deposit on the ground,” an advisory states. “Lead is toxic to humans and animals.”

noticias.titulo: Trump hosts third crypto gala for meme coin amid conflict of interest outcry
noticias.resumen: Virginia dinner comes as Democrats accuse president of improperly profiting from his cryptocurrency ventures Donald Trump is scheduled to headline his third cryptocurrency gala on ⁠Sunday night at his ​country club in Virginia, rewarding top holders of his own meme coin as Democrats accuse the president of improperly profiting from his crypto ventures. The dinner, set to take place at the Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, will include meet-and-greets with Trump supporters including the boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, Shark Tank investor Kevin O’Leary, NBA champion Tristan Thomp
noticias.texto:
Donald Trump is scheduled to headline his third cryptocurrency gala on Sunday night at his country club in Virginia, rewarding top holders of his own meme coin as Democrats accuse the president of improperly profiting from his crypto ventures.
The dinner, set to take place at the Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, will include meet-and-greets with Trump supporters including the boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, Shark Tank investor Kevin O’Leary, NBA champion Tristan Thompson and mentalist Lior Suchard, according to the event’s website.
The gala’s access and perks are divided by tiers for the 185 holders of $TRUMP, the president’s meme coin. A Trump fragrance, a poster, a “commemorative” ticket, and a “Trump watch” are reserved for 120 attendees. Meanwhile, the top 29 investors are invited to a VIP reception, and the top four will receive a “TRUMP 18K Gold Watch”.
Trump has hosted two similar galas since he took office last year, bringing a flurry of criticism as Democrats accuse Trump and his family of monetizing his brand through an array of equities and crypto ventures while in office.
After sweepingwins in the midterms, Democrats have vowed to investigate conflicts of interest involving Trump and his personal wealth during his presidency. They also say they plan to push for legislation that would ban activities such as the meme coin gala dinner.
“This dinner and scoring mechanism appear carefully constructed to increase investment in $TRUMP, allowing the President to abuse the power of his office to personally enrich himself, as he has throughout this term,” reads a letter sent by Adam Schiff and eight other US senators last month.
Since returning to the White House, Trump has made more than $1bn from his crypto businesses, according to financial disclosures released in June. Trump received more than $500m from his World Liberty Financial business selling new crypto products, and raked another $600m from sales of souvenir-type “meme” coins stamped with Trump’s face. Trump launched his $Trump meme coin days before his inauguration.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Interest in the $TRUMP coin dinner has plummeted, with contestants’ combined holdings dropping from $148m in May 2025 to $8.6m in this month’s gala.
More than half of the digital wallets publicly listed on the contest leaderboard for Sunday’s dinner are tied directly to crypto exchanges that bar US-based users, indicating they are linked to foreign nationals, according to an analysis of blockchain data prepared for Reuters by the nonpartisan, non-profit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen.
“Neither the President nor his family has ever engaged — or will ever engage — in conflicts of interest,” White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told Reuters earlier this year. “President Trump proudly made the United States the crypto capital of the world through executive actions.“
The Trump family’s other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also fallen in value to record lows. Together, outside investors in their five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5bn, according to a Reuters analysis.
The Trump meme coin has earned the Trump family at least $635m, according to the president’s June financial disclosure statement. In total, the Trumps had earned at least $2.3bn through April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin.
The president’s stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $430m.
Reuters contributed reporting

noticias.titulo: Abdul El-Sayed doubles down on ‘TrumpCare’ health plan, urging president to ‘get it done’
noticias.resumen: Democratic senator-elect reiterates suggestion to rename Medicare for All after Trump if president allows bill to pass Michigan US senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday doubled down on naming healthcare reform legislation after Donald Trump as long as it meant the president would not impede its passage. “If he’s open to the conversation, I am open to it, too,” El-Sayed said of Trump on Sunday. “If the president is opening to signing that bill, let’s get it done.” Continue reading...
noticias.texto:
Michigan US senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday doubled down on naming healthcare reform legislation after Donald Trump as long as it meant the president would not impede its passage.
“If he’s open to the conversation, I am open to it, too,” El-Sayed said of Trump on Sunday. “If the president is opening to signing that bill, let’s get it done.”
El-Sayed made those remarks on Sunday on NBC’s Meet the Press, where he reiterated his pledge to pursue a single-payer, national healthcare program after the Democrat became the first Muslim person elected to the US Senate during the midterms earlier in November.
Trump’s Republican party is going to lose control of Congress for the second half of his second presidency. But the president has made clear his intention to wield his legislative veto powers whenever he sees fit.
Appearing on Sunday’s Meet the Press, El-Sayed said he would not mind Medicare for All – a big part of his campaign platform – being named “TrumpCare” as long as such a program came into existence.
“I care that the people of this country finally have the unmet promise of guaranteed healthcare in this country. And if the president is serious about leaving a lasting legacy, there is nothing better than the ultimate Trump card,” El-Sayed said to Meet the Press host Kristen Welker, making a double entendre for a term that – when the T is lowercase – also refers to a card that beats out others in card games.
El-Sayed told Welker that such a Trump card would be in effect “from the moment [people] are born to the moment that they pass away – that guarantees them the healthcare that has been so elusive in this country without premiums, co-pays and deductibles”.
The senator-elect’s comments come after he previously suggested to CNN that he is not above stroking Trump’s prodigious ego to get legislation passed – including by naming Medicare for All “TrumpCare”.
He also previously wrote on social media, alongside images of a gold health insurance card with “TrumpCare” inscribed on it: “Donald, this is on the table. Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave.”
Trump seemingly responded to El-Sayed’s post by reposting a screenshot of the senator-elect’s tweet. Trump has not formally responded to the push to create universal healthcare.
Trump has spent much of his second presidency trying to get as much as possible named after him – from institutions, physical buildings and currency.
El-Sayed also said that he supports healthcare reform proposed by Bernie Sanders, the progressive US senator.
Sanders’ proposal would create a single-payer system in which the federal government insures everybody, financed by an increase in taxes, while eliminating private insurance.
But El-Sayed said he is not focused on eliminating private insurance as an option, which Sanders aims to eliminate by having everything primary and preventive services to hospital stays covered under his proposed plan. Out-of-pocket costs on deductibles and co-pays – staples of the rapacious private insurance industry to which most Americans must resort – would also be eliminated under Sanders’ plan.
El-Sayed said he wants to “provide you basic public health insurance no matter who you are in this country” while being open to the idea of not taking alternative options away.
The senator-elect said he has a meeting on the books with JD Vance. El-Sayed would not share the agenda of the meeting, but he confirmed that the vice-president’s chief of staff contacted him after his election victory.

noticias.titulo: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
noticias.resumen: It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible.
noticias.texto:
Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
The death of Fiona, a beloved hippopotamus who captured hearts, has renewed calls to remind zoo visitors that animals can die from swallowing foreign objects.
Fiona, 9 years old, died Thursday after ingesting a hat that accidentally ended up in her habitat at the Cincinnati Zoo. The zoo said that the hat was lodged in the hippo's small intestine and surgery was not possible.
"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Cincinnati Zoo Director Dave Jenike said in a statement.
While deaths are rare, items such as coins, shoes and sunglasses frequently fall, and sometimes are tossed, into animal enclosures.
In 2024, 70 U.S. coins were successfully removed from an alligator at Omaha's Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium. And in 2025, a Komodo dragon ate a shoe that was thrown into its habitat at the Memphis Zoo. The shoe was removed and the dragon survived.
Dr. Gabriella Flacke, an associate veterinarian at Zoo Miami, said the zoo's staff have retrieved items such as cellphones from alligators.
"We've had to remove those items both endoscopically, which is basically putting a camera through the mouth and down into the stomach to grab and retrieve those items, or we've in a few cases had to do surgery where they were larger items that couldn't be removed that way," Flacke told NPR.
Recovering items from an alligator is easier than a hippo, she said. Unlike the alligator, which has a digestive system with one stomach divided into two parts, hippos have a multichambered stomach. This can make retrieving objects, such as the small hat that Fiona ingested, difficult, according to Dr. Jen Quammen, president of the American Veterinary Medical Association.
"It's not necessarily always the shape or size of the object, but it's maybe the twists and turns, metaphorically and physiologically, that things have to go through," Quammen told NPR.
Be aware that the animals have specialized dietary needs and requirements that caretakers provide them, Flacke said. She also asked visitors to follow zoo etiquette and not yell or throw objects at the animals.
"Anything that we bring that could inadvertently end up in the animal exhibit or somehow around the animal, try to just be mindful and not have your sunglasses on your head if you're leaning over and looking at something," she said. "If your child has a toy in its hand and you're walking around, it could just decide to throw the toy, whether it's thinking about that or not."
It's not just dangerous for zoo animals
Both Quammen and Flacke said people should not only be mindful of items that can harm animals at the zoo, but also what could hurt animals in the wild or pets at home.
Animals explore the world by putting things in their mouths, making them naturally curious about items that can be dangerous, Quammen said.
To help prevent an animal from ingesting something dangerous, one should dispose of their trash and properly store items such as human medicines in a place where an animal cannot reach it.
"Don't feed an animal without permission and that includes our pets at home, but also wildlife," added Quammen.

noticias.titulo: What it's like at a climate conference as talks collapse
noticias.resumen: After two weeks of negotiations, international climate talks fail to reach an agreement. NPR's Rachel Waldholz was in Turkey for the conference.
noticias.texto:
What it's like at a climate conference as talks collapse
What it's like in the halls of a climate conference as it collapses
After two weeks of negotiations, international climate talks fail to reach an agreement. NPR's Rachel Waldholz was in Turkey for the conference.
ROB SCHMITZ, HOST:
International climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, ended today after negotiations fell apart. NPR's Rachel Waldholz has been at the conference and sent us this report.
RACHEL WALDHOLZ, BYLINE: I'm here in the Antalya Expo Center, which, for the past two weeks, has been packed with some 70,000 people who came to the COP31 climate conference. Now it's almost completely empty. In fact, they're disassembling parts of the venue around me. The climate talks ran two days past their scheduled end. By the time the gavel fell, many negotiators had already left to catch their flights home. Australia climate chief Chris Bowen led the negotiations.
CHRIS BOWEN: I haven't slept for the last three nights, been negotiating all the way through, but more importantly, people on delegations came at it and gave it everything they had.
WALDHOLZ: Delegates came to Antalya with long wish lists, from electrifying more of the global economy to money for developing countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change. Looming over it all is that this is the first summit to squarely face the reality that the planet will miss a key target of the Paris Climate Agreement, reaching warming of 1.5 degrees Celsius or 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit above pre-Industrial levels. The U.N. says limiting that overshoot requires cutting the use of fossil fuels nearly in half in the next 10 to 15 years. Many countries wanted an agreement explicitly calling for a transition away from coal, oil and natural gas. But big oil-producing countries, like Saudi Arabia, blocked any mention of fossil fuels. Ultimately, the European Union decided no deal was better than the deal on the table. Darragh O'Brien is Ireland's environment minister.
DARRAGH O'BRIEN: We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change.
WALDHOLZ: Many negotiators left the expo center dragging their suitcases on the way to the airport. They'll pick up negotiations next year at the next climate summit in Ethiopia. I'm Rachel Waldholz in Antalya, Turkey.
(SOUNDBITE OF SOFTLY'S "FLORA")

noticias.titulo: Philly festival-goers say pickles are a real big dill
noticias.resumen: Influencer and pickle enthusiast Dan Pancoast gives a first hand account of the festivities at the "The Big Dill" festival in Philadelphia.
noticias.texto:
Philly festival-goers say pickles are a real big dill
Love 'em or hate 'em, folks at a festival in Philly say pickles are a real big dill
Influencer and pickle enthusiast Dan Pancoast gives a first hand account of the festivities at the "The Big Dill" festival in Philadelphia.
ROB SCHMITZ, HOST:
We are now going to turn to pickles, a food that has seemed to follow me my whole life. When I was growing up, I used to watch my mom and grandma pickle cucumbers in the front yard. When I lived in China, every meal started with pao tsai, pickled vegetables. Then I moved to Germany and stumbled upon entire festivals devoted to the pickle. So I've been to places where people rave about pickles, but I've never been to a pickle rave. But we caught up with someone who has.
DAN PANCOAST: They had handed out, like, glow bracelets and glow necklaces, and everyone was just dancing and having a good time.
SCHMITZ: That is Dan Pancoast. Recently, he went to The Big Dill Pickle Festival, where they had a pickle rave. And...
PANCOAST: They have a brine chug. They give you a solo cup full of pickle brine. That was, like, the first thing that I put in my stomach today.
SCHMITZ: Pancoast is a content creator who lives in Pennsylvania, and he loves pickles.
PANCOAST: My tattoo is basically a dill pickle with a sombrero on, wearing sunglasses.
UNIDENTIFIED ANNOUNCER: It is National Pickle Day in Philadelphia, everybody.
(CHEERING)
PANCOAST: I walked up to the venue, and there was a good bit of people outside...
UNIDENTIFIED ANNOUNCER: Who's ready for the parade of pickles?
PANCOAST: ...Probably a couple hundred people wearing pickle hats, pickle shirts, sweatshirts, costumes.
UNIDENTIFIED ANNOUNCER: So the Grand Gherkin is here to help lead us.
PANCOAST: Now they're doing the world record parade. People dressed as pickles (laughter). It's quite amazing, honestly.
UNIDENTIFIED ANNOUNCER: To clear the space for the count.
SCHMITZ: Pancoast said the festival exceeded his expectations. It was a sort of picklepalooza (ph).
PANCOAST: And no matter what kind of pickles you love, what style, what you like your pickles on, don't like your pickles on, how you eat them, everyone can just be here. There's no real - anything else to think about. You can't really overthink it (laughter).
SCHMITZ: That was Dan Pancoast. The Big Dill Festival did, in fact, break the record for people dressed like pickles - 1,597 pickled people.
