noticias.titulo: Morocco: A surreal sculpture park turns the world upside down
noticias.resumen: An upside-down house, giant furniture and vegetable-headed figures await visitors at Ramakech, an 11-hectare sculpture park near Marrakech, where French artist Jean-François Fourtou brings childhood memories to life through extraordinary, larger-than-life installations.
noticias.texto:
One of its most striking attractions, The House Fallen from the Sky, was created in 2010 as a tribute to the artist's grandfather. Resting on its roof at a 17-degree angle, the house contains inverted furniture, windows and bathroom fittings, creating a disorientating experience for visitors. Elsewhere, enormous chairs, tables, notebooks and wardrobes invite guests to rediscover the world from a child's perspective.
The park also features farmers and gardeners with oversized pumpkin and plant-shaped heads, giant ants surrounding a mud-built structure, and colourful architectural installations. Fourtou says these unusual combinations of human and botanical forms are designed to provoke curiosity and unease, while his oversized household objects recreate the sensations he experienced as a young child exploring his great-grandmother's home. The artist began transforming the site in 1999, before opening it to the public in 2024. Today, Ramakech attracts around 5,000 visitors annually. For Fourtou, the sculptures are less about nostalgia than exploring emotions, family relationships and the memories that shape our understanding of the world.

noticias.titulo: Surging left-wing Basque separatists brace for showdown with Spain’s right
noticias.resumen: The left-wing EH Bildu coalition is set to perform strongly in the Basque Country — setting it on a potential collision course with a right-wing government in Madrid.
noticias.texto: Spain’s impending general election is set to reshape politics not only in Madrid but also in the northern industrial region of the Basque Country, where the bitterly divisive question of independence is boiling up again. A right-wing coalition is on course to form Spain’s next government after the Nov. 29 vote, but polls in the Basque region project a strong electoral performance by the left-wing separatist EH Bildu coalition. The two camps appear to be on a politically combustible collision course. Bildu’s rise has mirrored the Basque Country’s own transformation. Over the past decade, the rugged coastal region of 2.2 million people has increasingly shed its association with ETA, the separatist militant group that waged a decades-long campaign of violence before disbanding in 2018. As the shadow of political violence has receded, the Basque Country has consolidated its position as one of Spain’s most politically progressive and economically dynamic regions. It is now internationally recognized as an economic powerhouse — energy giant Iberdrola and banking group BBVA are both headquartered in Bilbao — and a global destination for high-end gastronomy. “The majority of the Basque Country is socially progressive and sovereigntist,” Gorka Elejabarrieta, a Bildu lawmaker running for the Spanish parliament in Gipuzkoa, told POLITICO. “Our coalition and movement bring together those two ideas, which are hegemonic in Basque society.” Spain’s political right has long opposed Basque separatism, but its hostility toward EH Bildu is particularly pronounced. It regards the party as “ETA’s heir” and has repeatedly questioned its legitimacy as an actor in democratic politics. Challenging the old order Within the Basque Country, this month’s election is also a contest to determine who will shape the region’s relationship with Madrid and its political future, with the resurgent Bildu challenging the decades-long dominance of the center-right Basque Nationalist Party (PNV). For the past 45 years the PNV has taken a pragmatic approach to regional autonomy. Closely tied to the region’s all-important business community — the comparatively wealthy Basque Country represents about 6% of Spain’s economy — it has sought to preserve economic stability for the region in its dealings with the national government. But Bildu has chipped away at the PNV’s dominance by appealing to both pro-independence voters and a broader left-wing electorate. Center-right figures such as People’s Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo — Spain’s expected next prime minister — and Madrid’s conservative regional president, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, frequently link Bildu to ETA and use its parliamentary agreements with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez to attack his legitimacy elsewhere in Spain. But ETA’s deadly legacy has receded as a concern for Basque voters. Some 15 years after the group ended its armed campaign, polling indicates terrorism no longer figures among the public’s main concerns, with housing, employment and health care taking precedence. SPAIN NATIONAL PARLIAMENT POLL OF POLLS All 3 Years 2 Years 1 Year 6 Months Smooth Kalman For more polling data from across Europe visit POLITICO Poll of Polls . That shift benefits Bildu, which has lately focused its messaging on quality-of-life policies. A late-October poll by the Basque government’s Sociological Prospection Office projected that Bildu will win seven of the 18 seats allocated to the Basque Country in Spain’s parliament. The PNV is forecast to take just four — its worst result in a general election since Spain’s return to democracy — and fall short of the five MPs needed to form its own parliamentary group. Elejabarrieta said a strong result would strengthen the party’s hand in pressing Madrid for a new settlement recognizing the Basque Country’s status as a nation and its right to decide its future. That, however, is where Bildu could find itself crossing swords with a government formed by the PP and the far-right Vox party. Elejabarrieta said his party would fight any attempts to curtail the Basque Country’s linguistic rights or autonomy. “If they attack us, if they try to undercut our self-government or sabotage our political activity, they will encounter a wall — not just from EH Bildu, but from Basque society as a whole,” he said. From social policy to sovereignty Between 1968 and 2010, ETA’s campaign for independence from Spain claimed the lives of 853 people . Months after the group announced a “definitive cessation of its armed activity” in 2011, Bildu emerged as a new vehicle for Basque nationalism, uniting pro-independence, radical-left groups that included former members of Batasuna — a banned party closely associated with ETA — with more moderate nationalists and figures from the non-nationalist left. Political scientist Eva Silván said Bildu began “a conscious and real evolution” after a sizeable number of Basque voters unexpectedly backed the left-wing Podemos party in 2015, “revealing there was an electorate in the Basque Country that was left-wing but not tied to nationalism or independence.” Bildu has courted those voters by focusing on social and economic measures championed by progressive and green-left parties across Europe. Silván said that shift has allowed the party to present itself as a “fresh” option alongside the PNV, which she said was viewed as out of touch with the concerns of younger voters. “Independence has not disappeared from its ideology, but it no longer occupies a prominent place in its agenda,” she said. Elejabarrieta acknowledged Bildu had shifted its focus toward issues affecting voters’ everyday lives, but stressed it had not abandoned its “openly sovereigntist and independentist” commitments. “For us, the social struggle and the national struggle are two sides of the same coin,” he said. The PNV is not blind to Bildu’s success with the Basque Country’s increasingly left-wing electorate, and has sought to counter portrayals of itself as old-fashioned. In a recent interview with the Onda Cero radio network, party leader Aitor Esteban said the PNV — which has historically maintained close ties with the Catholic Church — was “very progressive on social issues,” while acknowledging that it remained “very traditional” on economic matters. Aitor Esteban speaks at the Spanish parliament in Madrid on May 31, 2018. | Oscar del Pozo/AFP via Getty Images That balancing act is exemplified by the party’s position on housing: While it backed legislation to protect vulnerable families from eviction, it voted against measures to automatically extend existing rental contracts, arguing they would hurt small landlords. Esteban has repeatedly questioned the accuracy of gloomy polls, pointing to small sample sizes and large numbers of undecided voters. Privately, however, people in the PNV have been more candid about the challenge, with one party insider recently telling Spanish newspaper El Diario : “We’re fucked.” Awakening a pro-independence giant Elejabarrieta said if Sánchez is reelected, EH Bildu would be keen to continue working with his government on progressive legislation, including the minimum-income and rent-control measures introduced during the current term, while also exploring “ambitious” options for the Basque Country’s future. But a PP-led government in Madrid would be a different story. The center-right party wants to reinforce the central state’s presence in the Basque Country by expanding its administrative, police and military footprint, and has proposed dissolving parties that promote independence or illegal referendums — a central plank of Bildu’s political mission. The party also wants to restore Spanish as the language of debate in Spain’s parliament and scrap the interpretation and translation service for Basque and other co-official languages. The far-right Vox party, which the PP will likely need as a coalition partner, similarly aims to dismantle much of the Basque Country’s autonomy and has explicitly called for Bildu to be outlawed . Silván warned that a PP-Vox government could sharply polarize the region’s politics and reignite dormant tensions. “The Basque Country is a place where people still mobilize on the streets, and you can bet that trade unions and common people will stand up,” she said. Elejabarrieta said Bildu was acutely aware of the threat a possible right-wing government in Madrid would pose to “our national institutions, our language and our self-government,” and said the prospect had reinforced his party’s commitment to working with other progressive forces. He likened the current situation to that of the Basque government ruled by PNV leader José Antonio Aguirre during the Spanish Civil War. Aguirre led a coalition of center-right Basque nationalists, left-wing Spanish republicans and communists while besieged by Francisco Franco’s forces. “Just as they did in 1936, we now face an exceptional situation, and we must respond exceptionally and together,” he said. Elejabarrieta also warned that any attempt to undermine Basque self-government, institutions or national symbols would swell support for independence in both Catalonia and the Basque Country. “If they go down that road, we will soon become an enormous factory for pro-independence supporters,” he predicted.

noticias.titulo: Far right wants to transform the EU after big national election wins
noticias.resumen: Patriots’ co-president Kinga Gál says her political family’s immediate mission is helping its parties win national elections.
noticias.texto: BRUSSELS — Europe’s far right wants to reshape Brussels in the 2029 European Parliament election, after winning power in national capitals next year, the leader of the Patriots for Europe group told POLITICO. “The most important thing now for the Patriots group … is to help our parties back home to win elections and to govern because then they can bring the change … at the level of the [European] Council,” Hungarian MEP Kinga Gál said in her first interview since becoming co-president of the far-right group last month. Next year there are elections in France, Italy and Poland that could dramatically alter the political landscape in the EU. Before that, voters in Spain go to the polls in a week. After that, Gál said, “we have to see” how to strengthen ties between all the right-wing forces in the Parliament — the Patriots (home of Marine Le Pen’s National Rally), the European Conservatives and Reformists (of Giorgia Meloni’s Brothers of Italy) and the Europe of Sovereign Nations (of the Alternative for Germany). The ideal would be “to grow into a huge group,” Gál said of the three factions on the right of the parliamentary chamber, but “cooperation can have different forms.” However, they must move “step by step,” she said, adding that the Patriots must first see if “we get strengthened” in the national elections. Sitting in her corner office in the European Parliament in Brussels, Gál, a member of Viktor Orbán’s Fidesz party, said the center-right European People’s Party, the biggest in the Parliament, must take note of the surge in support for the far right. The firewall that once existed in Brussels to keep out the far right has already been breached, with the EPP passing key legislation with the support of far-right votes. The center-right has so far avoided structured cooperation in Brussels and barred far-right parties from positions of power, although in some capitals national parties have sealed coalition deals with the far right. Gál said she expects the EPP to scrap the firewall completely in the next few years and that the Patriots are now too big to ignore. “It cannot be that you treat millions of voters as second-class voters,” she said. The Hungarian MEP voiced optimism that Vox (which is in the Patriots group) would enter government in Spain after the Nov. 29 election. The center-right Popular Party, an EPP member, is on course to win the election but may need Vox’s support to govern . Gál added she was hopeful that Le Pen would become French president next May, and that Poland’s Law and Justice — which has flirted with joining the Patriots but remains a member of the ECR — would return to power in the autumn of 2027. Kinga Gál at a press conference during a plenary session at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France on Oct. 20, 2026. | Romeo Boetzle/AFP via Getty Images Gál has been co-president of the Patriots group alongside French National Rally leader Jordan Bardella since Oct. 20, after acting as first vice-president since 2024. While Bardella draws much of the attention, Gál does the legwork in Brussels. A focus on Brussels The Patriots’ national delegations remain guided largely by domestic interests, but Gál said the group provides a forum for coordinating messages and sharpening the pitch to voters. The strategy for the next few years is to focus on key priorities that attract voters, including tougher action on migration and borders, boosting the economy, and cutting energy costs. Gál said the bigger goal was to curb the power of the European Commission and return competences to member countries. She also did not dismiss AfD leader Alice Weidel’s proposal of abolishing direct European Parliament elections and replacing elected MEPs with delegates appointed by national parliaments. “These ideas, they all have their own validity” and need to be discussed, said Gál, adding that “it’s important to see how we conceive the future of Europe.” Gál routinely meets with Patriots’ leaders before European Councils in Brussels, including Le Pen, Czechia’s Andrej Babiš, Spain’s Santiago Abascal, Italy’s Matteo Salvini and Flanders’ Tom Van Grieken. Gál said that the one Patriots member in the European Council, Babiš, briefs those who may “very soon” be around the Council table on the agenda and important fights going on inside the room, while the leaders discuss their positions in order to close ranks. She said this helps Babiš “strengthen his position” and show “that we are behind him on many of the important issues.” On the EU long-term budget, for example, the Patriots leaders see eye to eye on keeping cash for farmers and regions, as well as disagreeing on new EU taxes and on “sending more money to Ukraine.” Asked whether the Patriots could seek to remove Ursula von der Leyen if they get more power in the Council, Gál said: “Yes. We tried to do it here in the Parliament,” referring to two failed no-confidence motions submitted over the last two years. But she said it’s not up to her to tell national leaders what to do in the Council.

noticias.titulo: Congo warns that EU countries’ Rwanda deportation deal could fund armed militia
noticias.resumen: EU countries are "making an informed choice to look the other way," Kinshasa's foreign affairs minister tells POLITICO.
noticias.texto: EU countries’ plans to send failed asylum-seekers to Rwanda risk fueling violent conflict and forced migration in Africa, according to the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Rwanda stands accused of supporting rebel forces that have taken control of large areas of eastern Congo, resulting in thousands of deaths and hundreds of thousands being displaced, the United Nations has said. Kinshasa fears the new migration plan will allow Rwanda to funnel European money to the rebels and “divert attention from [the country’s] destabilizing role in the Great Lakes region,” according to Congo’s Foreign Affairs Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner. “It is puzzling to see that a country that is at the heart, not just of instability, not just of conflict, but also of displacement and forced migration, is perceived to be a safe haven and … a credible partner to uphold international law,” Wagner told POLITICO. “The issue here is that we have [EU] countries that have the means, the access, [and] the capacity to know better, making an informed choice to look the other way,” Wagner added, telling EU countries to “go back to their notes” and rethink the choice of partner. The government of Rwanda did not respond to a request for comment. Last week, five countries — Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands — announced they will set up a deportation hub in Rwanda. While talks are ongoing, the five countries plan to start sending people to Rwanda in 2027. It’s part of a broader push by the bloc to gain greater control over who enters the EU — and who gets to stay. EU legislation approved earlier this year allows countries to negotiate such deals, as long as they safeguard fundamental rights. The announcement led to an outcry from rights groups, which warned that Kigali’s human rights record should disqualify it from such a partnership. Rwanda, besides having “a well-established record of repressing dissent,” also “provides critical support to and exercises overall control over the M23 armed group in eastern Congo,” NGO Human Rights Watch said this week . M23 occupies large swathes of North and South Kivu provinces in eastern Congo, having ramped up hostilities in early 2025 with a major offensive to capture Goma, the capital of North Kivu. The violence has displaced hundreds of thousands and the fighting around Goma alone left thousands dead . “Rapes, gang rapes, violent assaults and killings of civilians are a common feature of M23’s modus operandi,” U.N experts said. Kigali has repeatedly denied supporting the rebels, but the U.S., U.N. and EU have all called on Rwanda and its army to halt support for M23 and withdraw troops from Congo. Last month, the U.S. announced sanctions on Rwanda’s defense ministry and a financial institution over support for the armed group. Because of the U.S. sanctions, “there is a need for currency to come into the country. And it’s very convenient that the [EU countries] will be filling that gap,” Wagner said. “Why invest in a country that is violating the territorial integrity of another country?” M23 soldiers are seen in Goma, Democratic Republic of Congo on Feb. 6, 2025. | Alexis Huguet/AFP via Getty Images “Our cooperation with Rwanda to establish a return hub has no bearing on the German government’s position regarding the conflict in eastern Congo,” said Christina Lewinsky, a spokesperson for German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt. Denmark’s foreign affairs ministry said the country’s “position on the situation in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains unchanged,” and pointed to a statement dated Oct. 30 by the International Contact Group for the Great Lakes region (of which Denmark is a member) calling for a “lasting and peaceful resolution” to the conflict. Governments of Austria, Greece and the Netherlands didn’t respond to requests for comment. Denmark and Greece are both non-permanent members of the U.N. Security Council, which in a resolution last year demanded that Rwanda’s defense forces stop supporting M23, and also called on Congo’s military forces to halt support for armed groups. Announcing the partnership with Rwanda, ministers from the five EU countries repeatedly stressed that the protection of people sent to the country would remain a key priority and that the hub would be in line with EU and international law. Rwanda, they said, “has established itself as a reliable and responsible partner in addressing the global challenges of migration and forced displacement.” Rwanda’s Interior Minister Vincent Biruta took a similar line at a migration conference in Vienna last week. “Human rights in Rwanda are respected and granted to everyone and specifically to refugees who choose to come to our country,” he said, hitting back at protests by NGOs against the return hub deal . He stressed that his country already hosts thousands of refugees, including from Congo and Burundi. Congo’s Wagner said her country houses thousands of Rwandan refugees who “have not felt safe to return,” adding that those numbers “dwarf the number of refugees that are hosted by Rwanda .”

noticias.titulo: In the new world order, Europe doesn’t have a seat at the table
noticias.resumen: The meeting between Trump, Putin and Xi in Shenzhen last week offered few concrete results, but its symbolism underscored the continent’s waning influence.
noticias.texto: Jamie Dettmer is associate editor and a foreign affairs columnist for POLITICO . Winston Churchill had a bleak assessment of a 1943 summit in Tehran, where he, U.S. President Franklin Roosevelt and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin discussed wartime strategy and the shape of Europe after the war. “There I sat with the great Russian bear on one side of me with paws outstretched, and, on the other side, the great American buffalo,” the British prime minister recounted. “Between the two sat the poor little English donkey.” At least the poor little donkey was allowed in the room. Last week’s first-ever U.S.-Russia-China trilateral meeting in Shenzhen has been compared by some to a later meeting in Yalta, where Churchill, Stalin and Roosevelt hammered out the postwar order that’s now just about clinging on for survival. And yet, this time Europe’s diplomatic influence was nowhere to be seen. In the run-up to his August 2025 summit with Putin in Alaska, U.S. President Donald Trump at least consulted with major European leaders. But before Shenzhen, there was no wide consultation or virtual group huddle with European allies, according to two senior European officials who were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media. In short, as Trump met with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese premier Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, Europe was frozen out. To be sure, Shenzhen was no Yalta. Europe wasn’t on the table to be carved up by the American buffalo, Russian bear and Chinese panda. “At Yalta, Europe was divided up. It was parceled up. And we won’t allow anything like that to happen again,” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said in a lengthy press conference in Berlin flanked by other European leaders hours after the talks. “The meeting in Shenzhen was apparently a photo opportunity,” he added. And at first glance, maybe that’s right. When Trump was asked by Fox News what headline he wanted to come out of the summit, he lingered on the pomp and spectacle and on Xi personally receiving him at the airport, a rare move for the Chinese president. “It was a great respect and I appreciate that,” he said. “That’s a big win for us. That’s a big win for China, too. We get along.” “The trilateral summit was all image, no substance,” concurred Melanie Hart, a former senior adviser on China at the U.S. State Department and now at the Atlantic Council. Trump is greeted by Xi upon his arrival in Shenzhen on Nov. 18, 2026. | Pool photo by Mandel Ngan via Getty Images Certainly, the summit produced few concrete results. The trio pledged to push for reform of the U.N. and to “increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations” — a notable win for Putin, as it presumably means Trump won’t enforce energy sanctions on Russia. They also said “that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction,” in effect reaffirming the immunity of state officials from international courts and institutions. Another win for Putin, who’s wanted on an ICC arrest warrant. And they said a nuclear war must never be fought. For Natia Seskuria of the RUSI think tank in London, “the ‘new Yalta’ did not happen in Shenzhen as the three leaders had very different agendas.” “Trump wanted to be seen as a great dealmaker,” she said. “Putin wanted to be seen as an equal great power, back on the world stage. Xi took the credit for hosting them both without signing up to either man’s agenda.” And yet, it would be a mistake to dismiss what happened in Shenzhen as irrelevant or something that won’t have long term consequences. The summit will likely be assessed in the future as another step away from the post-Cold War liberal international order and a return to much more unabashed and ruthless great power politics — where big states lord it over smaller ones, brushing off international norms, including efforts to end impunity for leaders accused of war crimes. In short it signaled the likely direction of travel. That can only continue to widen the divide between Washington and its European allies. Indeed, another hint of the emerging world order was on display hours after the talks concluded, when Trump called from Air Force One into the Berlin meeting of Ukraine’s European allies to express vigorous skepticism about Europe spending further billions in aid to Ukraine after Putin had told him he really wants a peace deal. “Trump would have no qualms about deciding on Ukraine’s fate without Ukraine at the table,” said Fredrik Wesslau, a former U.N. and EU diplomat and now at the European Council on Foreign Relations. “He has shown that he does not care about European security or Ukraine but rather about normalizing relations with Russia so that narrow financial interests close to him can make money,” he added. Wesslau holds out hope that the “multi-polar world of great powers, spheres of interest, and buffer zones will hit the reality of resistance from smaller states — as Russia has learnt in Ukraine.” Maybe so, maybe not. At Yalta, Churchill at least managed to finagle one or two things, including successfully getting France a permanent seat on the U.N. Security Council along with Britain. That would help strengthen Europe’s diplomatic influence, Churchill thought. It did for a while. But times have changed.

noticias.titulo: Lucy Powell promotes UK education in China despite risks
noticias.resumen: The U.K. education secretary's visit to Beijing comes days after Wes Streeting praised the government for stepping up its interaction with China.
noticias.texto: LONDON — Education Secretary Lucy Powell will travel to Beijing this week to promote closer ties between schools and universities in the two countries, as the U.K. government makes a fresh push for high-level engagement with China. She will take part in a U.K.-China summit — the first for nine years — aimed at helping British educational institutions and businesses build new links with Beijing. The trip is expected to expand opportunities for British providers of vocational training, overseas campuses, online learning and the export of educational materials such as textbooks, learning platforms and classroom supplies. Powell’s visit comes days after Defence Secretary Wes Streeting hosted his Chinese counterpart, Dong Jun, in London. Streeting praised Andy Burnham’s government for having “stepped up our interaction with China.” Powell said ahead of the summit that education was one of Britain’s “greatest strengths” and “expanding that internationally is a massive opportunity for our economy and wider society.” She vowed to use it to “support growth, strengthen our global standing and stand up for what matters to Britain.” Closer cooperation on education will form part of “clear-eyed engagement with China” by the government, she said, as she promised to champion freedom of speech and academic freedom during her trip. Her efforts to promote British education abroad come despite the security services warning about the scale of Chinese attempts to spy on the U.K. More than 100 academics linked to British institutions have unwittingly assisted China’s espionage operations by taking funding from a Chinese spy agency, MI5, the U.K.’s domestic intelligence agency, revealed in September . Powell specified that she would seek to “protect U.K. institutions from any collaborations that could undermine national security, or attempts to benefit covertly from research done in partnership with U.K. universities.” U.K. officials said the trip would recognize the contribution of the 150,000 Chinese students currently studying at U.K. universities rather than actively seeking to invite more.

noticias.titulo: Costa gives Macron early Christmas present on EU budget
noticias.resumen: Governments have criticized European Council President António Costa's proposal on the bloc's 7-year budget for leaning toward France.
noticias.texto: BRUSSELS — Emmanuel Macron heads into a summit of EU leaders on Thursday emboldened by winning crucial concessions on the bloc’s next 7-year budget , as governments privately signaled optimism about reaching a deal on the spending plan in December. The outgoing French president emerged as the beneficiary of the latest proposal that European Council President António Costa unveiled on Saturday. Leaders will tussle over the framework at their gathering in Brussels. Even as it drew criticism from all sides ― including from the French themselves ― a budget plan that leans toward France signals a potential compromise because of the country’s position midway between the two main rival camps. The crown jewel for Macron was Costa’s plan to raise money for the EU budget from a tax on tech multinationals — a French pet project shelved in 2018 over fears of U.S. retaliation. In further concessions to the French, Costa shielded farmers’ subsidies from cuts, proposed new taxes to cap national contributions to Brussels, and deferred €10 billion in payments of EU post-Covid debt. Underscoring the complex nature of the debate, Fabienne Keller, an MEP from Macron’s Renaissance party, said the digital tax proposal was “ good news ” but that the cuts overall “undermine Europe’s ambitions” and “clip its wings.” Costa’s latest proposal for the budget ― worth roughly €1.78 trillion and due to start in 2028 ― is €44 billion smaller than the version that Ireland , in its role holding the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU, presented last month. Governments are split between those wanting a smaller budget geared toward modern priorities like defense and competitiveness, and those demanding the EU spend more and focus on traditional areas such as farming and poorer regions. Despite the wide disagreements, Costa and most governments are determined to get a deal by the end of the year. “Seems like Santa Claus came early this year for the French,” said one EU diplomat who, like others quoted in this story, was granted anonymity to speak freely about the sensitive negotiations. ‘Deeply disappointing’ Costa’s move in Macron’s direction represents a rare win in the twilight of the latter’s presidency. The beleaguered French leader steps down in May, and faces the prospect of being succeeded by far-right Eurosceptic Marine Le Pen or left-wing populist Jean Luc Mélenchon ― one of the main reasons the EU wants to get a deal on the budget this year. Costa and Macron enjoy a close working relationship, according to several diplomats, and share similar ambitions for European spending. They “have the same strategy of focusing on new own resources [taxes] and postponement of NextGenEU [post-Covid debt] as issues that should be solved before the end game,” said a second diplomat. Still, governments are gearing up for some tough negotiating ahead. In a classic display of political theatrics, the French president’s office criticized Costa’s proposal as “deeply disappointing” and said it “doesn’t provide a basis for an agreement.” That, too, could be a tactic, with the French renowned for driving a hard bargain and, as another EU diplomat said, wanting to win each match 10-0 rather than settle for a smaller victory. “Don’t really understand the Elysée criticism,” one of the diplomats said. “They basically got what they wanted.” Farmers protest France’s gripe with Costa’s proposal is that the cuts are excessive while the guarantees for farmers — a powerful constituency with high stakes in the EU budget — are insufficient. That claim was echoed by powerful farmer lobby Copa Cogeca, which announced a protest in Brussels on the day of the leaders’ summit. Police officers watch tractors during a farmers’ protest in Brussels on Dec. 18, 2025. | Nicolas Tucat/AFP via Getty Images But other governments were quick to call Paris’ bluff. They noted that Costa had preserved €297 billion in direct payments to farmers and had turned a loosely defined “rural” spending target into fresh money for agriculture. “With every new [budget proposal] comes a new goodie for agriculture and a further cut to modernization,” said a third EU diplomat from a country whose contributions to the budget exceed their payouts. Despite the grumbling, diplomats who spoke to POLITICO exuded greater optimism that Costa will succeed in shepherding the EU’s 27 countries toward a final agreement by the end of the year — before elections in France, Italy and Poland that threaten to derail the talks. Countries need a deal among themselves before seeking agreement with the European Parliament. In a statement on Saturday , German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed the need to end negotiations “before the end of 2026.” Le Pen ‘fearmongering’ Despite the cuts — which affect almost all spending items except farmers’ subsidies — the proposed budget remains about 25% larger in real terms than the 2021-2027 Multiannual Financial Framework, although a large part of the increase is due to repayments of post-Covid debt. Throughout the negotiations Macron has pushed for more EU-wide taxes, known as own resources, to generate extra revenue and limit France’s contributions to Brussels, which are the second largest after Germany’s. In a concession to Paris, Costa largely preserved the total revenue projections of around €60 billion from the Commission’s proposal last year. He also devised a workaround to push back some payments — and save billions of euros in the next budget cycle — by extending the timeline over which capitals must spend their share of regional funds by one year. According to Costa, this will limit the rise in national contributions from 0.80% to 0.82% of the countries’ gross national incomes — a key priority also for other net payers, known as the frugals, including Germany and the Netherlands. Nevertheless, the concessions might still not be enough for the hardline frugals to accept a deal by the end of the year. “There is still a sense of rather no deal than a bad deal,” said the first EU diplomat. “The fearmongering about Le Pen is not taken seriously in the frugal camp.”

noticias.titulo: How Big Oil and the Trump administration outwitted Brussels to delay an EU climate law
noticias.resumen: Intense lobbying prompted the EU to delay plans to force fossil fuel companies to report their methane emissions.
noticias.texto: How Big Oil and the Trump administration outwitted Brussels to delay an EU climate law Intense lobbying prompted the EU to delay plans to force fossil fuel companies to report their methane emissions. By BEN MUNSTER in Brussels Illustration by Natália Delgado / POLITICO EU bureaucrats spent much of the past year fending off a full-frontal lobbying campaign to delay a key plank of the European Green Deal. They fought hard — but in the end they couldn’t outmaneuver the fossil fuel industry. After seven hours of chaotic debate Thursday, EU member countries and lawmakers agreed to delay by two years a landmark law that would force importers of oil and gas to the bloc to monitor and eventually reduce emissions of the greenhouse gas methane. Expelled in vast volumes from leaky pipes and wells and vented into the atmosphere at production sites across the globe, the super-pollutant is the second-biggest contributor to global warming, trapping as much as 86 times more heat than carbon dioxide pound-for-pound over a 20-year period. The agreement Thursday was a triumph for the Brussels fossil fuel lobby and its allies in Washington, which for over a year were able to convince a significant number of member countries and lawmakers that the rules could lead to serious supply disruptions if implemented by the scheduled January 2027 deadline. The campaign seized on existing anxieties over prices and supply that had sprung up in the wake of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, forcing institutional defenders of the rules to agree to a delay they never believed was necessary. The move puts the EU’s efforts to be a global climate leader in doubt at a time when countries are retreating from environmental commitments worldwide. While the obligations on importers will technically be reinstated in 2029, the terms of the revised timeline give governments latitude to delay further. Smoke and flames rise after an airstrike in Tehran on March 7, 2026. | Majid Saeedi/Getty Images “Put it in your diary: 2029, we’re going to have the same conversations about how we’re not ready and we can’t have this legislation ever brought in,” said Seb Kennedy, an LNG analyst and the founder of gas and LNG intelligence platform Energy Flux. It was the nuance in industry’s position — and the mind-bendingly confusing way in which EU regulation is drafted — that gave the campaign its claws. Unlike national laws that are proposed by governments and approved by legislators, EU rules require the support of three separate bodies — the Council, which represents member countries, the Parliament, and the Commission, the bloc’s executive. The three-way talks between these groups that take place before rules are adopted can result in eleventh hour compromises that can make regulation difficult to adopt in practice. So it was with the methane rules. The original proposal mainly regulated domestic producers, and many of the obligations on international importers were only added toward the end of inter-institutional negotiations that ran several years before the law was adopted in 2024. That transformed a largely local regulation into one with global scope, with EU officials promising to hash out the details at a later date. As the months wore on without any clarification on key provisions for verifying emissions, member countries said they were unable to fully implement the rules, leaving companies uncertain whether their imports would be compliant when the January deadline came. While the EU executive insisted the law was clear enough for governments to figure out the finer points of the legislation for themselves — capitals, after all, had insisted on this approach when the law was agreed — industry figures despaired at what they described as a policy mess. But for months, the EU executive offered little detail, and lobbyists got no traction. Then the Iran war set their campaign ablaze. U.S. Ambassador to the EU Andrew Puzder, who became the White House’s go-to critic of EU rules, gives an interview in Brussels on Apr. 9, 2026. | Nicolas Tucat/AFP via Getty Images In March, as oil and gas prices were beginning to shoot up while Iranian bombs and drones struck tankers and gas fields in the Persian Gulf, the International Organization of Oil & Gas Producers invited reporters to the presentation of an industry-backed study by Edinburgh-based energy consultancy Wood Mackenzie. The study warned that failure to put the methane rules on hold could leave broad swaths of Europe’s supply non-compliant, risking as much as 87% of its oil imports and 43% of its natural gas imports — vital fuels that increasingly come from the U.S. From the outset, the Commission never bought this dire assessment. Internally, officials believed that the rules as written were clear and blamed member countries for being slow to transpose them, according to people familiar with the matter. They held up a countervailing study by Norwegian consultancy Rystad, funded by the Environmental Defense Fund, an environmentalist nonprofit, which suggested that more than enough of the EU’s supply would be compliant. Pressure from industry intensified. In Brussels alone, fossil fuel executives brought up the rules at dozens of in-person meetings with senior officials . National companies — including French oil giant TotalEnergies — lobbied their own ministries. At the request of energy firms , U.S. officials got increasingly involved, dispatching diplomats to member countries and issuing thundering denunciations of the regulation on social media. The complaints began to really gain traction with the intervention of senior officials from a Trump administration bent on a policy of “energy dominance” over Europe. U.S. Ambassador to the EU Andrew Puzder became the White House’s go-to critic of the rules in Brussels, weighing in regularly on social media and in media op-eds to call for a delay. “The EU’s Methane Regulation risks triggering another energy crisis,” Puzder posted in April 2026, exactly two months after the U.S. started bombing Iran. “The EU must fix the regulation’s core defects or risk driving away its most dependable suppliers — decreasing energy supplies while increasing energy costs. American LNG is reliable, low-emission, and ready to scale. The U.S. stands ready to provide the reliable energy Europe needs.” All the while, critics of the rules stressed that they had no issue with the ambitions of the regulation itself. Fossil fuel firms said they were only bothered by the compliance challenges, pointing to voluntary industry efforts to bring down emissions that preceded the adoption of the EU rules. Puzder praised the goals of the rules in an op-ed for the Financial Times, trumpeting the U.S.’s own advances in bringing down emissions. But the messaging wasn’t always consistent. A report earlier this month by EUobserver unearthed a post by IOGP Director Francois-Regis Mouton de Lostalot from September 2025 that appeared to contradict the advocacy group’s support for the principle of methane reduction, with the Frenchman welcoming the opportunity to work with the U.S. to “address and remove regulatory barriers” like the Methane Regulation. The comments came after Mouton de Lostalot spoke at an event featuring senior officials from the Trump administration, which itself moved to kill Biden-era methane rules last month. “That was a quick comment typed on a phone,” Mouton de Lostalot told POLITICO. “I meant fixing specific provisions in the file, not scrapping the Regulation altogether.” He said the IOGP has supported the objectives of the regulation since “day one,” pointing to the dozens of statements it has made over the last five years. The campaign continued. The lobbying efforts even took one diverse group of European Parliament members all the way to Texas, where lawmakers were welcomed to the Houston HQ of LNG titan Cheniere and given a tour of ExxonMobil’s methane monitoring system. In both cases, executives criticized the methane rules, according to a readout of the trip and an MEP who attended the trip and was granted anonymity to discuss it candidly. That MEP told POLITICO that they had barely followed the file before embarking on the trip, but were left with the impression that serious supply disruptions could occur if a delay wasn’t introduced, and that oil and gas exporters may even stop selling to Europe to avoid non-compliance. The lawmaker added that they were also swayed to support a delay by an ExxonMobil ad that appeared in one of POLITICO’s newsletters. National governments — led by Czechia and Slovakia — soon cottoned on, corralling like-minded countries to pressure the Commission to delay the rules. In open letters, statements and media interviews , ministers echoed industry’s assessment of the supply risks and its appeal for a delay. Håkon Fonseca Nordang, a Brussels-based spokesperson for IOGP, defended the use of industry material by EU officials, which he said may not have been necessary “if an impact assessment on the importer requirements had been conducted earlier.” In the “informational vacuum” that resulted from institutional dithering, “having scenarios modeled by a credible consultancy is critical,” he added. EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen arrives for a meeting in Brussels on March 16, 2026. | Nicolas Tucat/AFP via Getty Images With political pressure growing as energy supplies were squeezed by the war with Iran, the Commission faced a dilemma. The institution’s energy chief, Dan Jørgensen, had invested significant political capital in defending the rules, repeatedly pledging never to reopen them. But a concession would have to be made to the regulation’s critics, and EU officials figured that genuine anxieties around energy prices would allow them to address industry and member country concerns while minimizing the perception of climate backsliding, people familiar with the executive’s position told POLITICO. The Commission’s first proposal was to allow countries to suspend enforcement of penalties for three years. Industry kept complaining, and in September — after a dramatic intervention by French President Emmanuel Macron at a moment of acute pressure in diesel markets — Jørgensen proposed delaying the rules by a single year. But that meant allowing lawmakers and member countries to negotiate the file for the second time in two years. The risk was they would attempt to impose deeper changes on the rules, as they had with other green laws over the preceding two years. That’s pretty much what happened. The ensuing negotiations quickly became a debate over how much further to extend the delay, with center-right lawmakers allying with far-right lawmakers to push for a postponement of three years, while governments endorsed one year with a recurring “review clause” that EU officials worried would have allowed for indefinite delay. In the closed-door talks Thursday, Jørgensen held fast, arguing that the supply risks had been overstated and that one year was more than enough, according to people who were in the room, granted anonymity to speak openly. But supporters of a longer delay appeared spooked by the prospect of market disruptions, citing warnings made by supplier countries, according to Jutta Paulus, a Greens MEP who was also in the room. In the end, they agreed to a two-year delay. The following day, IOGP welcomed the pause. “We are proud of the role we played,” said Fonseca Nordang, the spokesperson. The advocacy group will now focus on “supporting industry on the technical side and through standardization work, but also through input and support to the Commission and Member States on the regulatory implementation side,” he added. Outside of the Brussels bubble, close watchers of European energy markets were left disappointed. “Of all the things that move the needle, the methane regulation was right there at the very bottom,” said Kennedy, the LNG analyst. “The methane regulation was never really a realistic supply-side constraint,” he said. “And yet it seems to have been so stunningly successful in capturing the imagination of European policymakers.”

noticias.titulo: Thousands rally in Istanbul against Turkey’s crackdown on opposition and media
noticias.resumen: Thousands marched in Istanbul on Sunday against a widening crackdown on Turkey’s opposition and independent media, days after police raided Sozcu TV and arrested senior staff. The main opposition Yeni Parti organised the protest after authorities installed a government-appointed trustee at the broadcaster, following similar moves against other independent outlets.

noticias.titulo: Sánchez vaticina en 'Salvados' su victoria: "Mis datos tienen buena pinta, no suelo autoengañarme"
noticias.resumen: El presidente del Gobierno dice: "Cómo pase a la historia se lo dejo a los historiadores, yo estoy centrado en el 29 de noviembre".
noticias.texto: El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez , se ha mostrado este domingo convencido de la victoria del PSOE en las elecciones , ya que sostiene que maneja unos datos "que tienen muy buena pinta" , explica en la entrevista que ha concedido al programa de LaSexta Salvados . Todo empezó cuando el presentador del espacio, Fernando González 'Gonzo' le preguntó cómo cree que sería recordado. "Cómo pase a la historia se lo dejo a los historiadores, yo estoy centrado en el 29 de noviembre" , respondió Sánchez, que vaticinó después su victoria. Sobre este particular, Gonzo le preguntó si, llegado el momento, sería capaz de abstenerse para que un ganador Feijóo no tuviera que pactar una investidura con Vox. Sánchez replicó que eso no iba a ocurrir, porque el PSOE iba a ocurrir: "Vamos a ganar, vamos a ser primera fuerza política y vamos a gobernar con una mayoría progresista más amplia que la que hemos tenido en esta última legislatura. Lo digo claro a siete días de las elecciones", ha vaticinado. Ante la confianza mostrada, el presentador le preguntó en qué basaba una afirmación tan rotunda: "Tengo mis datos, no suelo autoengañarme, y tienen muy buena pinta", respondió Sánchez, que agregó que aunque se pueda equivocar, no ha visto una movilización como la actual en las cinco anteriores citas electorales a las que se ha presentado. No aceptará un referéndum en Cataluña Por otro lado, Sánchez ha asegurado que no concedería la celebración de un referéndum de autodeterminación en Cataluña tras las elecciones, aunque necesite los votos de las formaciones independentistas para volver a gobernar. No lo hará, según ha asegurado, porque la Constitución no lo permite y porque esa medida iría en contra de la política de "convivencia" que ha desplegado en Cataluña desde que es presidente. Sánchez, que negaba la amnistía a los líderes del procès antes de las pasadas generales de julio de 2023 y la acabó aceptando al necesitar los votos de Junts para ser presidente, dice que en esta ocasión no podría hacerlo porque "no entra dentro del marco constitucional". "En segundo lugar, yo diría que es todo lo contrario a lo que hemos venido haciendo durante todo este tiempo, que es normalizar la convivencia, cohesionar a la sociedad catalana y por tanto no dividirla", ha señalado a continuación. En ese sentido presume de que los partidos soberanistas ahora no hablan de la independencia de Cataluña sino de asuntos que están dentro de la Carta Magna c omo la financiación autonómica, o la situación de servicios públicos como Rodalíes. En todo caso ha reiterado que "por supuesto" que no aceptaría llevar a cabo un referéndum de autodeterminación aunque esta sea la condición para volver a gobernar cuatro años más. Al ser interrogado sobre por qué deberían de creerle ahora los ciudadanos si hace cuatro años negó que fuese a aprobar la amnsitía y luego lo hizo, dice que "además de la palabra también están los hechos" y en el tiempo que lleva siendo presidente ha "respetado la Constitución". A renglón seguido ha aprovechado para lanzar un dardo al PP, señalando que cuando gobernaban ellos "sí se produjeron referéndums de autodeterminación" en referencia a la votación del 1 de octubre de 2017 y el Gobierno de entonces, presidido por Mariano Rajoy "no sabían ni donde estaban las urnas" con la que los organizadores llevaron a cabo las votaciones.

noticias.titulo: El Gobierno enviará un requerimiento a la Comunidad de Madrid para revocar la orden que pide neutralidad a los profesores
noticias.resumen: El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha comparado estas instrucciones de la Consejería de Educación con un formulario de censura del franquismo.
noticias.texto: El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez , ha anunciado este domingo que el Ejecutivo enviará un requerimiento a la Comunidad de Madrid para que revoque la orden dirigida por la Consejería de Educación madrileña a los centros educativos públicos no universitarios, y que establecen medidas de neutralidad al profesorado durante la huelga de los docentes. A través de un mensaje compartido en redes sociales, Sánchez ha justificado esta medida al considerar que esas instrucciones de la Comunidad de Madrid " atentan contra uno de los derechos más importantes del profesorado". En este sentido, el jefe del Ejecutivo ha comparado con la publicación de dos imágenes estas directrices de la Comunidad con un formulario de censura durante la dictadura franquista . En concreto, en este último documento se censuraba el comportamiento del maestro republicano Antonio Benaiges en la localidad de Bañuelos de Bureba, en la provincia de Burgos. "El de la izquierda es un formulario de denuncia con el que el franquismo perseguía y censuraba la libertad ideológica. El de la derecha, el formulario con el que la Comunidad de Madrid pretende hacer lo mismo en pleno siglo XXI. No es un fake. No es una exageración. Es la represión volviendo a nuestras vidas ", ha expresado Sánchez antes de anunciar el requerimiento que enviarán al Gobierno regional. El pasado jueves, la Comunidad de Madrid dictó dos instrucciones dirigidas a los centros educativos públicos no universitarios para garantizar la neutralidad institucional y docente durante las huelgas. Las instrucciones, firmadas por el viceconsejero de Política y Organización Educativa, José Carlos Fernández Borreguero, establecen que "el centro docente público es de todos y debe ser neutral " y subrayan que "su función es educar, no adoctrinar". En concreto, la Consejería prohíbe al profesorado "transmitir a los alumnos sus opiniones políticas, ideológicas , partidistas o sindicales con el fin de que las compartan", así como utilizar clases, tutorías, exámenes o actividades complementarias para ganar su apoyo a alguna de las partes de un conflicto. Tampoco se podrá animar a los estudiantes a participar en huelgas , manifestaciones o recogidas de firmas, ni realizar comentarios o señalamientos ante alumnos o familias sobre compañeros que secunden los paros o decidan trabajar. Ambas directivas comenzaron ya a aplicarse desde el pasado viernes, han confirmado desde el comité de profesores que secunda la huelga indefinida en la enseñanza pública madrileña. Los sindicatos que conforman el comité han calificado estas instrucciones como un "ataque contra el derecho de huelga" . Además, han aseverado que el Gobierno regional ha "hostigado" a los docentes desde el comienzo de la misma, "insultando al profesorado en lucha", "despreciando" sus reivindicaciones, "ignorando al comité de huelga" y, en última instancia "elevando el tono y pasando a las amenazas, denuncias e instrucciones como estas".

noticias.titulo: Raquel Bollo planta cara a Cristina Porta en 'GH VIP' y menciona a Aguasantas: "Ha venido a tocarme la pingoleta"
noticias.resumen: Aguasantas, expareja de su hijo Manuel Cortés, centró un cruce en el que también salió a relucir el padre de su nieta.
noticias.texto: Raquel Bollo tuvo otro cruce con Cristina Porta en la casa de GH VIP , y esta vez el nombre propio fue el de Aguasantas , expareja de su hijo Manuel Cortés. Según Raquel, su compañera la había mencionado delante de ella, y no estaba dispuesta a dejarlo pasar en silencio. La discusión llegó a la casa con el reproche ya preparado. Raquel acusó a Cristina de ir "de rama en rama" y de generar conflictos allí por donde pasaba. Después le pidió cuentas directamente por lo que había dicho. "¿Tú crees que yo no me he dado cuenta de lo que has dicho?", le preguntó, y dejó claro que seguía el hilo de cada comentario. La concursante respondió a su manera: nombrando ella también a Aguasantas. " La nombro para que vea que no tengo problema ", explicó, convencida de que así le quitaba a Cristina cualquier ventaja. Y recordó el contexto que, según ella, todo el mundo conoce. "Sabiendo todo el mundo los problemas que yo he tenido", añadió. Entonces señaló una contradicción. Aguasantas es hoy la pareja de Juan José Peña, expareja de Alma Bollo y padre de la nieta de Raquel, y Raquel no entendía que se hablara de unos y no de otros. " El padre de mi nieta, que ha hecho un reality, es anónimo ", denunció, y comparó su situación con la de su propia pareja, que no ha salido en ningún medio. Raquel cerró el cruce poniendo su edad por delante. " Ha venido a tocarme la pingoleta, pero tengo ya 51 años ", sentenció, y con esa frase dio por terminada la discusión. Cristina Porta no es la primera concursante con la que choca desde que empezó el programa.

noticias.titulo: Isabel Allende y los seis días en que supo que su hija Paula se iba: "Se sabe cuándo viene la muerte"
noticias.resumen: Un silo vacío, una nieta nacida nueve meses después y un año de coma: la escritora, en 'Cuarto Milenio'.
noticias.texto: Javier Pérez Campos llevó a Cuarto Milenio una conversación con Isabel Allende sobre el año más oscuro de su vida . En 1991, su hija Paula , que se había casado ese mismo año, sufrió una crisis de porfiria y fue ingresada en Madrid. Tras la medicación que le administraron, descrita en el programa como una negligencia médica, quedó con daño cerebral y en coma durante un año. La escritora abordó el desenlace sin rodeos. "Tengo cierta familiaridad con la muerte porque primero murió Paula en mis brazos, que es lo peor que le puede pasar a una madre, y después mi madre y después mi padrastro", explicó. Paula estaba en coma y no podía reaccionar, pero Allende notó un cambio en ella antes de que nadie se lo dijera. " Unos 6 días antes supe que se iba a morir ", aseguró, y precisó que conocía incluso el día y la noche. Su explicación fue breve: "Se sabe cuándo viene la muerte", añadió. El aviso, según contó, había llegado en forma de sueño. En él aparecía un silo vacío, con granos flotando en el aire y palomas, y su hija con 12 años. "Y de repente Paula empezaba a levitar, a levantarse", recordó, y ella intentaba sujetarla del abrigo para subir con ella. " El sueño era clarísimo: que Paula se me iba y yo no me podía ir con ella", concluyó. Nueve meses después de perder a Paula nació Nicole, la última nieta de la escritora. " Paula murió en mis brazos y Nicole nació en mis brazos ", recordó Allende, que fue quien cortó el cordón umbilical. Al recibir a la recién nacida, con la idea de que venía del mismo lugar al que se había ido su madre, le pidió: "Nicole, cuéntame cómo era antes que se te olvide".

noticias.titulo: El incendio de un bus con 12 personas dentro en la calle Biada de Barcelona afecta a varios edificios sin causar heridos
noticias.resumen: Un autobús de la línea 39 arde en Gràcia sin causar heridos; una familia con un bebé permanece fuera de su vivienda tras el suceso
noticias.texto: Un autobús con 12 pasajeros se ha incendiado este domingo a última hora de la tarde en la calle Biada , en la confluencia con Torrent de l'Olla, en el barrio de Gràcia de Barcelona . Las llamas, ya extinguidas, han afectado al menos a un edificio próximo sin causar heridos, según han informado fuentes municipales. Los equipos de emergencia han revisado y ventilado cuatro fincas y dos locales en la zona afectada, permitiendo el regreso a sus viviendas de la mayoría de los residentes, salvo una familia que no ha podido volver por precaución. Un bus urbano se incendia en Barcelona y el fuego afecta a varias fincas cercanas EFE Doce pasajeros y el conductor lograron salir a tiempo; las llamas alcanzaron inmuebles próximos y obligaron a movilizar diez dotaciones Se trata de una familia con un bebé de pocos meses a la que se ha recomendado esperar antes de regresar al domicilio. Han sido atendidos por el Servicio de Urgencias y Emergencias Sociales de Barcelona. Los bomberos, que movilizaron 10 dotaciones , recibieron el aviso a las 20.01 y sofocaron el fuego del autobús a las 20.49. Los bomberos descartan con "una probabilidad muy alta" que haya más personas afectadas en el accidente del autobús Europa Press El siniestro deja 83 personas atendidas, siete graves y 34 menos graves; los equipos de rescate revisarán el vehículo antes de retirarlo con una grúa de gran tonelaje Tecnología de gas El vehículo, completamente calcinado, pertenecía a la línea 39 , medía alrededor de 12 metros y operaba con tecnología de gas . El incendio se originó en la parte delantera a la altura del número 1 de la calle Biada. El conductor evacuó a todo el pasaje y, por ahora, se desconoce el motivo del fuego , que será analizado por ingenieros este lunes.

noticias.titulo: Heridas dos personas en un accidente múltiple con un camión en Boborás (Ourense)
noticias.resumen: El siniestro obligó a desplegar un amplio operativo, incluido un helicóptero, para liberar a los afectados
noticias.texto:
Heridas dos personas en un accidente múltiple con un camión en Boborás (Ourense)
El siniestro obligó a desplegar un amplio operativo, incluido un helicóptero, para liberar a los afectados
Dos personas han resultado heridas en un accidente múltiple en Boborás (Ourense), registrado entre Noqueira y Brués, en el que se vio implicado un camión. Ambas quedaron atrapadas y tuvieron que ser liberadas por los Bomberos de O Carballiño.
Según informó el 112 Galicia, un particular dio la alarma alrededor de las 17.30 horas de este domingo. En su aviso, señalaba la participación de varios vehículos, entre ellos un camión, y la posible presencia de personas atrapadas tras la colisión.
Al lugar acudió un amplio dispositivo formado por efectivos de Urgencias Sanitarias de Galicia 061, los Bomberos de O Carballiño, el GES de Ribadavia, la Guardia Civil y personal de mantenimiento de carreteras. También se activó el helicóptero medicalizado con base en Ourense.
La alcaldesa de la localidad, Patricia Torres, trasladó a los medios que dos personas fueron excarceladas por los bomberos y sufrieron heridas en el siniestro. Una de ellas fue evacuada finalmente en helicóptero medicalizado.

noticias.titulo: Un motorista resulta herido grave al chocar con un coche en la zona de Ayacata (Gran Canaria)
noticias.resumen: El afectado sufrió varios traumatismos y fue evacuado en helicóptero al Hospital Universitario Insular tras el siniestro registrado en Gran Canaria
noticias.texto:
Un motorista resulta herido grave al chocar con un coche en la zona de Ayacata (Gran Canaria)
El afectado sufrió varios traumatismos y fue evacuado en helicóptero al Hospital Universitario Insular tras el siniestro registrado en Gran Canaria
Un motorista ha resultado herido de gravedad tras colisionar alrededor de las 14.00 horas de este domingo con un coche en la GC-60, a la altura de Ayacata y dentro del término municipal de San Bartolomé de Tirajana (Gran Canaria).
El Centro Coordinador de Emergencias y Seguridad (Cecoes) 112 indicó que, tras recibirse el aviso, se activó un helicóptero medicalizado y una ambulancia de soporte vital básico del Servicio de Urgencias Canario (SUC). En el punto del siniestro, los sanitarios atendieron al afectado, que presentaba múltiples traumatismos de carácter grave. Fue estabilizado y evacuado al Hospital Universitario Insular de Gran Canaria.
Además, bomberos de San Bartolomé de Tirajana aseguraron la maniobra de toma de tierra y el posterior despegue del helicóptero en el campo de fútbol de Tunte, y prestaron apoyo al resto de los intervinientes. Por último, agentes de la Guardia Civil asumieron la instrucción del atestado correspondiente.

noticias.titulo: Trump se «inclina» por reanudar los ataques contra Irán si no hay acuerdo para Año Nuevo
noticias.resumen: El presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, ha afirmado este domingo que se «inclina» por reanudar los bombardeos sobre Irán si finalmente no se logra un acuerdo diplomático […]
noticias.texto:
Trump se «inclina» por reanudar los ataques contra Irán si no hay acuerdo para Año Nuevo
El republicano se ha referido a la intención de poner a prueba el bloqueo naval estadounidense en el golfo Pérsico
El presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, ha afirmado este domingo que se «inclina» por reanudar los bombardeos sobre Irán si finalmente no se logra un acuerdo diplomático para Año Nuevo, como recoge Europa Press.
«El presidente ha dicho a Fox News que se inclina por reanudar los ataques contra Irán si tras Año Nuevo no se ha logrado un acuerdo», ha explicado el jefe de corresponsales de la cadena estadounidense, Trey Yingst. El periodista ha explicado que Trump le ha confirmado que las negociaciones continúan con un formato indirecto, pero los iraníes son «bailarines de claqué profesionales. No paran de hablar. No hacen más que hablar, pero todo es pura palabrería», ha indicado.
Trump también se ha referido a las informaciones sobre la intención de Irán de poner a prueba el bloqueo naval estadounidense en el golfo Pérsico y ha reiterado que hay un bloqueo vigente sobre los puertos iraníes. «Espero que lo hagan. Si intentan atravesar el bloqueo estadounidense acabarán en el fondo del mar, como el resto de la Armada iraní», ha asegurado.

noticias.titulo: Sánchez dice que no aceptará un referéndum en Cataluña aunque necesite los votos de Junts o ERC para gobernar
noticias.resumen: El presidente del Gobierno y candidato del PSOE a la reelección, Pedro Sánchez, ha asegurado que no concedería la celebración de un referéndum de autodeterminación en Cataluña tras las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre, aunque necesite los votos de las formaciones independentistas para volver a gobernar.
noticias.texto:
MADRID, 22 Nov. (EUROPA PRESS) -
El presidente del Gobierno y candidato del PSOE a la reelección, Pedro Sánchez, ha asegurado que no concedería la celebración de un referéndum de autodeterminación en Cataluña tras las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre, aunque necesite los votos de las formaciones independentistas para volver a gobernar.
No lo hará, según ha asegurado este domingo en un entrevista en el programa 'Salvados' recogida por Europa Press, porque la Constitución no lo permite y porque esa medida iría en contra de la política de "convivencia" que ha desplegado en Cataluña desde que es presidente.
Sánchez --que negaba la amnistía a los líderes del procès antes de las pasadas generales de julio de 2023 y la acabó aceptando al necesitar los votos de Junts para ser presidente-- dice que en esta ocasión no podría hacerlo porque "no entra dentro del marco constitucional".
"En segundo lugar, yo diría que es todo lo contrario a lo que hemos venido haciendo durante todo este tiempo, que es normalizar la convivencia, cohesionar a la sociedad catalana y por tanto no dividirla", ha señalado a continuación.
En ese sentido presume de que los partidos soberanistas ahora no hablan de la independencia de Cataluña sino de asuntos que esán dentro de la Carta Magna como la financiación autonómica, o la situación de servicios públicos como Rodalíes.
DEBEN CREERLE PORQUE HA RESPETADO LA CONSTITUCIÓN
En todo caso ha reiterado que "por supuesto" que no aceptaría llevar a cabo un referéndum de autodeterminación aunque esta sea la condición para volver a gobernar cuatro años más.
Al ser interrogado sobre por qué deberían de creerle ahora los ciudadanos si hace cuatro años negó que fuese a aprobar la amnsitía y luego lo hizo, dice que "además de la palabra también están los hechos" y en el tiempo que lleva siendo presidente ha "respetado la Constitución".
A renglón seguido ha aprovechado para lanzar un dardo al PP, señalando que cuando gobernaban ellos "sí se produjeron referéndums de autodeterminación" en referencia a la votación del 1 de octubre de 2017 y el Gobierno de entonces, presidido por Mariano Rajoy "no sabían ni donde estaban las urnas" con la que los organizadores llevaron a cabo las votaciones.
ENTREVISTA "EXÓTICA" DE PUIGDEMONT
Así, sobre la reciente entrevista concedida por el expresidente catalán y dirigente de Junts, Carles Puigdemont, en la que calificó a Sánchez como una persona "amoral" y con una "ambición desmedida", el jefe del Ejecutivo dice que le sorprendió su publicación, el mismo día del debate con Alberto Núñez Feijóo y la calificó de "exótica". "Además en El Mundo, me parece todo un poco raro", ha apostillado.
En todo caso ha criticado que la derecha dé credibilidad a las afirmaciones de Puigdemont y las considere "palabra de Dios" porque le critican a él, mientras que "se la han negado cuando les ha interesado".
Además ha dicho que no aprobó la Ley de Amnistía "por Puigdemont" sino como "culminación" de un proceso de normalización de la convivencia en Cataluña que, defiende, ha tenido efectos positivos. Ahora la gente, dice, puede hablar de política y los catalanes van a apoyar "de manera mayoritaria" al PSOE en las elecciones del próximo domingo.

noticias.titulo: Atlético de Madrid regressa às vitórias e Guedes volta a marcar na La Liga
noticias.resumen: O Atlético de Madrid regressou hoje às vitórias na Liga espanhola, ao bater fora o Getafe (3-0), na 13.ª jornada, num dia em que Gonçalo Guedes marcou pela Real Sociedad, que perdeu por 3-2 em Santander.
noticias.texto:
Futebol Internacional
    
Atlético de Madrid regressa às vitórias e Guedes volta a marcar na La Liga
O Atlético de Madrid regressou hoje às vitórias na Liga espanhola, ao bater fora o Getafe (3-0), na 13.ª jornada, num dia em que Gonçalo Guedes marcou pela Real Sociedad, que perdeu por 3-2 em Santander.
No Coliseum Alfonso Pérez, em Getafe, nos arredores de Madrid, Álex Baena, aos 10 minutos, e Johnny Cardoso, aos 30, colocaram os ‘colchoneros’ em vantagem, antes do antigo jogador do Benfica Alejandro Grimaldo, de grande penalidade, aos 90+2, fixar o resultado final.
Após dois desaires consecutivos, diante do Bayern Munique e do FC Barcelona, os ‘colchoneros’ voltaram a vencer e seguem no terceiro posto da La Liga, com 31 pontos, a dois do Real Madrid, de José Mourinho, segundo, e a cinco do líder Barça.
Já a Real Sociedad, sofreu uma derrota na deslocação ao terreno do Racing Santander, apesar do golo do internacional português Gonçalo Guedes, que marcou pela terceira vez no campeonato espanhol.
O avançado português, que não marcava há cinco jogos consecutivos em todas as competições, fez o 2-2 aos 60 minutos, após os anfitriões terem construído uma vantagem de dois golos.
O marroquino Yassir Zabiri, antigo jogador do Famalicão, esteve em destaque ao ‘bisar’, aos seis e oito minutos, enquanto Mikel Oyarzabal reduziu para os bascos, em cima do intervalo (45+1). Sergio Canales, aos 68, de grande penalidade, garantiu o triunfo do conjunto da Cantábria.
A Real Sociedad ocupa o quinto lugar, com 22 pontos, a cinco do Betis, quarto, enquanto o Racing Santander é sétimo, com 17.
Nos restantes encontros do dia, o Osasuna venceu o Málaga por 1-0, depois de o FC Barcelona bater o Villarreal por 3-2, após uma reviravolta de dois golos, para segurar três pontos de vantagem na liderança de La Liga.

noticias.titulo: Inter desperdiça vantagens e empata 4-4 em Bérgamo em jogo de 'loucos'
noticias.resumen: O Inter Milão caiu hoje para o terceiro lugar da Liga italiana de futebol, após um jogo de ‘loucos’ em Bérgamo com a Atalanta (4-4), em que o campeão deixou fugir várias vantagens, no primeiro ‘hat-trick’ de Esposito.
noticias.texto:
Futebol Internacional
    
Inter desperdiça vantagens e empata 4-4 em Bérgamo em jogo de 'loucos'
O Inter Milão caiu hoje para o terceiro lugar da Liga italiana de futebol, após um jogo de ‘loucos’ em Bérgamo com a Atalanta (4-4), em que o campeão deixou fugir várias vantagens, no primeiro ‘hat-trick’ de Esposito.
Este duelo da 12.ª jornada promete ser sério candidato a melhor jogo da edição 2026/27 da Serie A, com o Inter a construir por três vezes uma diferença de dois golos no encontro, acabando a Atalanta nos descontos por salvar um ponto.
Francesco Esposito, avançado de 21 anos e esperança número um da seleção italiana (10 golos em 15 internacionalizações), assinou o primeiro 'hat-trick’ da carreira, enquanto na Atalanta o belga Charles De Ketelaere respondeu com um ‘bis’.
Esposito, aos 16 e 32 minutos, parecia encaminhar o Inter para o triunfo, com o macedónio Eljif Elmas a reduzir a diferença ainda antes do intervalo, aos 35, acabando o avançado italiano por aumentar novamente a vantagem, aos 52.
Charles De Ketelaere, aos 72 minutos, voltou a relançar a Atalanta na partida, mas o emblema de Milão respondeu com o 4-2 pelo croata Sucic, aos 75, de grande penalidade.
Aos 80 minutos, novamente Charles De Ketelaere a marcar, com o costa-marfinense Kessie, aos 90+1, em novo penálti, a fazer o 4-4 final.
Com este resultado, o Inter caiu para o terceiro posto, com 29 pontos, e ficou a um da Roma, que subiu a segundo, e a três da Lazio, que lidera. Logo atrás, em quarto com 27, a equipa de Chivu tem o AC Milan de Ruben Amorim.
Habituada nas últimas temporada aos lugares cimeiros, a Atalanta é apenas 12.º posicionada, com 15 pontos.

noticias.titulo: Benfica elimina detentor do título Torreense na quarta ronda da Taça de Portugal
noticias.resumen: O Benfica, recordista de vitórias na competição, com 26 troféus, afastou hoje o Torreense, da II Liga, da Taça de Portugal em futebol, ao bater fora os detentores do título por 3-1, na quarta eliminatória.
noticias.texto:
Taça de Portugal
    
Benfica elimina detentor do título Torreense na quarta ronda da Taça de Portugal
O Benfica, recordista de vitórias na competição, com 26 troféus, afastou hoje o Torreense, da II Liga, da Taça de Portugal em futebol, ao bater fora os detentores do título por 3-1, na quarta eliminatória.
No Estádio Nacional, casa emprestada dos vencedores da Taça de Portugal 2025/26, Jhon Durán, aos 30 minutos, Prestianni, aos 64, e Kaminski, aos 85, marcaram os golos dos ‘encarnados’, enquanto Musa Drammeh, aos 50, faturou para os ‘locais’.
Os ‘encarnados’, que não ganham a prova desde 2016/17, vão defrontar nos oitavos de final, em casa, entre 15 e 17 de dezembro, o Tondela, da II Liga, que no sábado bateu fora o igualmente ‘secundário’ AVS por 5-1.

noticias.titulo: Marselha deixa escapar vantagem de dois golos e perde com o Le Mans na Ligue 1
noticias.resumen: O Marselha desperdiçou uma vantagem de dois golos e perdeu hoje por 3-2 na receção ao Le Mans, na 11.ª jornada da Liga francesa de futebol, falhando a possibilidade de somar a sexta vitória consecutiva no campeonato.
noticias.texto:
Futebol Internacional
    
Marselha deixa escapar vantagem de dois golos e perde com o Le Mans na Ligue 1
O Marselha desperdiçou uma vantagem de dois golos e perdeu hoje por 3-2 na receção ao Le Mans, na 11.ª jornada da Liga francesa de futebol, falhando a possibilidade de somar a sexta vitória consecutiva no campeonato.
No Vélodrome, a equipa marselhesa, que vinha de cinco triunfos seguidos, parecia encaminhada para prolongar a série, depois de Amine Gouiri (33 minutos) e Igor Paixão (40) colocarem o Marselha a vencer por 2-0, ainda na primeira parte.
Contudo, o Le Mans reagiu na segunda parte e iniciou a recuperação aos 70 minutos, por Louis Mafouta. Erwan Colas restabeleceu a igualdade, aos 84, antes de Jean Vercruysse consumar a reviravolta, aos 90+5.
O Le Mans interrompeu assim uma série de cinco derrotas consecutivas e voltou a vencer no campeonato, algo que não conseguia desde 19 de setembro, quando bateu o Lorient por 2-1.
Já o Marselha, que tinha vencido o Lens por 2-1, em 08 de novembro, falhou a oportunidade de prolongar a série vitoriosa e aproximar-se dos primeiros lugares da classificação.
Antes, o Paris FC goleou o Angers por 4-0 e somou a terceira vitória consecutiva no campeonato, aproximando-se do líder Paris Saint-Germain, de quem está a três pontos.
Depois de uma primeira parte sem golos, Patrick Zabi inaugurou o marcador aos 47 minutos, seguindo-se os tentos de Luca Koleosho (55), Maxime Lopez (65) e Diego Coppola (72), que fixaram o resultado no Stade Jean-Bouin, em Paris.
Com esta vitória, o Paris FC aproveitou a derrota do Lille frente ao Lyon (1-0), no sábado, para subir ao segundo lugar, reforçando a sua posição nos lugares cimeiros, enquanto o Angers prolongou para seis jogos a série sem vencer na Ligue 1, somando um empate e cinco derrotas.
Por seu lado, o Rennes continua sem reencontrar o caminho das vitórias, ao empatar 1-1 no terreno do Lorient, resultado que prolongou para três jogos a série sem triunfos da equipa, que contou com o português Gonçalo Oliveira no ‘onze’ inicial.

noticias.titulo: Marta Paço de novo campeã mundial de surf adaptado
noticias.resumen: A portuguesa Marta Paço sagrou-se hoje campeã do mundo da classe Vi1 no campeonato do mundo de surf adaptado, que está a decorrer em Palm Desert, na Califórnia.
noticias.texto:
Surf
    
Marta Paço de novo campeã mundial de surf adaptado
A portuguesa Marta Paço sagrou-se hoje campeã do mundo da classe Vi1 no campeonato do mundo de surf adaptado, que está a decorrer em Palm Desert, na Califórnia.
Esta é já a quinta vez que a surfista de Viana do Castelo, invisual, chega ao título mundial, depois de já o ter conseguido em 2021, 2022, 2023 e 2024.
Na final, Marta Paço, de 21 anos, superou a brasileira Ingrid Medina e francesa Valentine Moskoteoc logo na primeira ronda, com pontuações de 4,00, 2,50 e 1,87, respetivamente.
Na segunda ronda, a atleta vianense voltou a dominar as adversárias, juntando 2,83 pontos, contra 2,33 da brasileira e 2,77 da francesa.
As surfistas tiveram direito a duas ondas de direita e duas ondas de esquerda, sendo a classificação final determinada pelo somatório das melhores. Pela primeira vez, a competição realizou-se numa piscina de ondas, na DSRT Surf.
